p0004 text    . 1681 .
p0005 head    1
p0005 title   THE TRANSLATORS TO THE READER
p0005 text    {Preface to the King James Version of 1611}
p0005 text    {THE BEST THINGS HAVE BEEN CALUMNIATED}
p0005 text    Zeal to promote the common good, whether it be by devising anything ourselves, or
p0005 text    revising that which hath been laboured by others, deserveth certainly much respect
p0005 text    and esteem, but yet findeth but cold entertainment in the world. It is welcomed with
p0005 text    suspicion instead of love, and with emulation instead of thanks: and if there be any
p0005 text    hole left for cavil to enter, (and cavil, if it do not find a hole, will make one) it is sure to
p0005 text    be misconstrued, and in danger to be condemned. This will easily be granted by as
p0005 text    many as know story, or have any experience. For, was there ever any-projected, that
p0005 text    savoured any way of newness or renewing, but the same endured many a storm of
p0005 text    gainsaying, or opposition? A man would think that Civility, wholesome Laws, learning
p0005 text    and eloquence, Synods, and Church-maintenance, (that we speak of no more things of
p0005 text    this kind) should be as safe as a Sanctuary, and out of shot, as they say, that no man
p0005 text    would lift up the heel, no, nor dog move his tongue against the motioners of them. For
p0005 text    by the first, we are distinguished from brute beasts lead with sensuality; By the
p0005 text    second, we are bridled and restrained from outrageous behaviour, and from doing of
p0005 text    injuries, whether by fraud or by violence; By the third, we are enabled to inform and
p0005 text    reform others, by the light and feeling that we have attained unto ourselves; Briefly, by
p0005 text    the fourth being brought together to a parley face to face, we sooner compose our
p0005 text    differences than by writings which are endless; And lastly, that the Church be
p0005 text    sufficiently provided for, is so agreeable to good reason and conscience, that those
p0005 text    mothers are holden to be less cruel, that kill their children as soon as they are born,
p0005 text    than those nursing fathers and mothers (wheresoever they be) that withdraw from
p0005 text    them who hang upon their breasts (and upon whose breasts again themselves do hang
p0005 text    to receive the Spiritual and sincere milk of the word) livelihood and support fit for
p0005 text    their estates. Thus it is apparent, that these things which we speak of, are of most
p0005 text    necessary use, and therefore, that none, either without absurdity can speak against
p0005 text    them, or without note of wickedness can spurn against them.
p0005 text    Yet for all that, the learned know that certain worthy men [Anacharsis with others]
p0005 text    have been brought to untimely death for none other fault, but for seeking to reduce
p0005 text    their Countrymen to god order and discipline; and that in some Commonwealths [e.g.
p0005 text    Locri] it was made a capital crime, once to motion the making of a new Law for the
p0005 text    abrogating of an old, though the same were most pernicious; And that certain [Cato
p0005 text    the elder], which would be counted pillars of the State, and patterns of Virtue and
p0005 text    Prudence, could not be brought for a long time to give way to good Letters and refined
p0005 text    speech, but bare themselves as averse from them, as from rocks or boxes of poison;
p0005 text    And fourthly, that he was no babe, but a great clerk [Gregory the Divine], that gave
p0005 text    forth (and in writing to remain to posterity) in passion peradventure, but yet he gave
p0005 text    forth, that he had not seen any profit to come by any Synod, or meeting of the Clergy,
p0005 text    but rather the contrary; And lastly, against Church-maintenance and allowance, in
p0005 text    such sort, as the Ambassadors and messengers of the great King of Kings should be
p0005 text    furnished, it is not unknown what a fiction or fable (so it is esteemed, and for no better
p0005 text    by the reporter himself [Nauclerus], though superstitious) was devised; Namely, that
p0005 text    at such a time as the professors and teachers of Christianity in the Church of Rome,
p0005 text    then a true Church, were liberally endowed, a voice forsooth was heard from heaven,
p0005 text    saying: Now is poison poured down into the Church, etc. Thus not only as oft as we
p0005 text    speak, as one saith, but also as oft as we do anything of note or consequence, we
p0006 head    2
p0006 text    subject ourselves to everyone’s censure, and happy is he that is least tossed upon
p0006 text    tongues; for utterly to escape the snatch of them it is impossible. If any man conceit,
p0006 text    that this is the lot and portion of the meaner sort only, and that Princes are privileged
p0006 text    by their high estate, he is deceived. “As the sword devoureth as well one as the other,”
p0006 text    as it is in Samuel [2 Sam 11:25], nay as the great Commander charged his soldiers in a
p0006 text    certain battle, to strike at no part of the enemy, but at the face; And as the King of Syria
p0006 text    commanded his chief Captains to “fight neither with small nor great, save only against
p0006 text    the King of Israel:” [1 Kings 22:31] so it is too true, that Envy striketh most spitefully at
p0006 text    the fairest, and at the chiefest. David was a worthy Prince, and no man to be compared
p0006 text    to him for his first deeds, and yet for as worthy as act as ever he did (even for bringing
p0006 text    back the Ark of God in solemnity) he was scorned and scoffed at by his own wife [2
p0006 text    Sam 6:16]. Solomon was greater than David, though not in virtue, yet in power: and by
p0006 text    his power and wisdom he built a Temple to the Lord, such a one as was the glory of the
p0006 text    land of Israel, and the wonder of the whole world. But was that his magnificence liked
p0006 text    of by all? We doubt it. Otherwise, why do they lay it in his son’s dish, and call unto him
p0006 text    for easing the burden, “Make”, say they, “the grievous servitude of thy father, and his
p0006 text    sore yoke, lighter?” [1 Kings 12:4] Belike he had charged them with some levies, and
p0006 text    troubled them with some carriages; Hereupon they raise up a tragedy, and wish in
p0006 text    their heart the Temple had never been built. So hard a thing it is to please all, even
p0006 text    when we please God best, and do seek to approve ourselves to every ones conscience.
p0006 text    If we will descend to later times, we shall find many the like examples of such kind,
p0006 text    or rather unkind acceptance. The first Roman Emperor [C. Caesar. Plutarch] did never
p0006 text    do a more pleasing deed to the learned, nor more profitable to posterity, for
p0006 text    conserving the record of times in true supputation; than when he corrected the
p0006 text    Calendar, and ordered the year according to the course of the Sun; and yet this was
p0006 text    imputed to him for novelty, and arrogance, and procured to him great obloguy. So the
p0006 text    first Christened Emperor [Constantine] (at the least-wise that openly professed the
p0006 text    faith himself, and allowed others to do the like) for strengthening the Empire at his
p0006 text    great charges, and providing for the Church, as he did, got for his labour the name
p0006 text    Pupillus, as who would say, a wasteful Prince, that had need of a Guardian or overseer
p0006 text    [Aurel. Victor]. So the best Christened Emperor [Theodosius], for the love that he bare
p0006 text    unto peace, thereby to enrich both himself and his subjects, and because he did not see
p0006 text    war but find it, was judged to be no man at arms [Zosimus], (though indeed he excelled
p0006 text    in feats of chivalry, and showed so much when he was provoked) and condemned for
p0006 text    giving himself to his ease, and to his pleasure. To be short, the most learned Emperor
p0006 text    of former times [Justinian], (at the least, the greatest politician) what thanks had he for
p0006 text    cutting off the superfluities of the laws, and digesting them into some order and
p0006 text    method? This, that he had been blotted by some to be an Epitomist, that is, one that
p0006 text    extinguishes worthy whole volumes, to bring his abridgments into request. This is the
p0006 text    measure that hath been rendered to excellent Princes in former times, even, Cum
p0006 text    bene facerent, male audire, For their good deeds to be evil spoken of. Neither is there
p0006 text    any likelihood, that envy and malignity died, and were buried with the ancient. No,
p0006 text    no, the reproof of Moses taketh hold of most ages; “You are risen up in your fathers’
p0006 text    stead, and increase of sinful men.” [Num 32:14] “What is that that hath been done?
p0006 text    that which shall be done; and there is no new thing under the Sun,” saith the wiseman:
p0006 text    [Ecc 1:9] and S. Stephen, “As your fathers did, so do you.” [Acts 7:51]
p0006 text    {HIS MAJESTY’S CONSTANCY, NOTWITHSTANDING CALUMNIATION, FOR THE SURVEY}
p0006 text    {OF THE ENGLISH TRANSLATIONS}
p0006 text    This, and more to this purpose, His Majesty that now reigneth (and long, and long
p0006 text    may he reign, and his offspring forever, “Himself and children, and children’s always)
p0007 head    3
p0007 text    knew full well, according to the singular wisdom given unto him by God, and the rare
p0007 text    learning and experience that he hath attained unto; namely that whosoever
p0007 text    attempteth anything for the public (especially if it pertain to Religion, and to the
p0007 text    opening and clearing of the word of God) the same setteth himself upon a stage to be
p0007 text    gloated upon by every evil eye, yea, he casteth himself headlong upon pikes, to be
p0007 text    gored by every sharp tongue. For he that medleth with men’s Religion in any part,
p0007 text    medleth with their custom, nay, with their freehold; and though they find no content
p0007 text    in that which they have, yet they cannot abide to hear of altering. Notwithstanding his
p0007 text    Royal heart was not daunted or discouraged for this that colour, but stood resolute, “as
p0007 text    a statue immovable, and an anvil not easy to be beaten into plates,” as one [Suidas]
p0007 text    saith; he knew who had chosen him to be a Soldier, or rather a Captain, and being
p0007 text    assured that the course which he intended made for the glory of God, and the building
p0007 text    up of his Church, he would not suffer it to be broken off for whatsoever speeches or
p0007 text    practices. It doth certainly belong unto Kings, yea, it doth specially belong unto them,
p0007 text    to have care of Religion, yea, it doth specially belong unto them, to have care of
p0007 text    Religion, yea, to know it aright, yea, to profess it zealously, yea to promote it to the
p0007 text    uttermost of their power. This is their glory before all nations which mean well, and
p0007 text    this will bring unto them a far most excellent weight of glory in the day of the Lord
p0007 text    Jesus. For the Scripture saith not in vain, “Them that honor me, I will honor,” [1 Sam
p0007 text    2:30] neither was it a vain word that Eusebius delivered long ago, that piety towards
p0007 text    God was the weapon and the only weapon, that both preserved Constantine’s person,
p0007 text    and avenged him of his enemies [Eusebius lib 10 cap 8].
p0007 text    {THE PRAISE OF THE HOLY SCRIPTURES}
p0007 text    But now what piety without truth? what truth (what saving truth) without the word
p0007 text    of God? What word of God (whereof we may be sure) without the Scripture? The
p0007 text    Scriptures we are commanded to search. John 5:39. Isa 8:20. They are commended
p0007 text    that searched and studied them. Acts 17:11 and 8:28,29. They are reproved that were
p0007 text    unskillful in them, or slow to believe them. Matt 22:29. Luke 24:25. They can make us
p0007 text    wise unto salvation. 2 Tim 3:15. If we be ignorant, they will instruct us; if out of the
p0007 text    way, they will bring us home; if out of order, they will reform us; if in heaviness,
p0007 text    comfort us; if dull, quicken us; if cold, inflame us. Tolle, lege; Tolle, lege, Take up and
p0007 text    read, take up and read the Scriptures [S. August. confess. lib 8 cap 12], (for unto them
p0007 text    was the direction) it was said unto S. Augustine by a supernatural voice. “Whatsoever
p0007 text    is in the Scriptures, believe me,” saith the same S. Augustine, “is high and divine; there
p0007 text    is verily truth, and a doctrine most fit for the refreshing of men’s minds, and truly so
p0007 text    tempered, that everyone may draw from thence that which is sufficient for him, if he
p0007 text    come to draw with a devout and pious mind, as true Religion requireth.” [S. August. de
p0007 text    utilitcredendi cap. 6] Thus S. Augustine. and S. Jerome: “Ama scripturas, et amabit te
p0007 text    sapientia etc.” [S. Jerome. ad Demetriad] Love the Scriptures, and wisdom will love
p0007 text    thee. And S. Cyril against Julian; “Even boys that are bred up in the Scriptures, become
p0007 text    most religious, etc. [S. Cyril. 7 contra Iulianum] But what mention we three or four
p0007 text    uses of the Scripture, whereas whatsoever is to be believed or practiced, or hoped for,
p0007 text    is contained in them? or three or four sentences of the Fathers, since whosoever is
p0007 text    worthy the name of a Father, from Christ’s time downward, hath likewise written not
p0007 text    only of the riches, but also of the perfection of the Scripture? “I adore the fulness of the
p0007 text    Scripture,” saith Tertullian against Hermogenes. [Tertul. advers. Hermo.] And again,
p0007 text    to Apelles an heretic of the like stamp, he saith; “I do not admit that which thou
p0007 text    bringest in (or concludest) of thine own (head or store, de tuo) without Scripture.”
p0007 text    [Tertul. de carne Christi.] So Saint Justin Martyr before him; “We must know by all
p0007 text    means,” saith he, “that it is not lawful (or possible) to learn (anything) of God or of
p0008 head    4
p0008 text    right piety, save only out of the Prophets, who teach us by divine inspiration.” So Saint
p0008 text    Basil after Tertullian, “It is a manifest falling way from the Faith, and a fault of
p0008 text    presumption, either to reject any of those things that are written, or to bring in (upon
p0008 text    the head of them) any of those things that are not written. We omit to cite to the same
p0008 text    effect, S. Cyril B. of Jerusalem in his 4::Cataches., Saint Jerome against Helvidius, Saint
p0008 text    Augustine in his 3::book against the letters of Petilian, and in very many other places
p0008 text    of his works. Also we forebear to descend to later Fathers, because we will not weary
p0008 text    the reader. The Scriptures then being acknowledged to be so full and so perfect, how
p0008 text    can we excuse ourselves of negligence, if we do not study them, of curiosity, if we be
p0008 text    not content with them? Men talk much of [an olive bow wrapped about with wood,
p0008 text    whereupon did hang figs, and bread, honey in a pot, and oil], how many sweet and
p0008 text    goodly things it had hanging on it; of the Philosopher’s stone, that it turned copper into
p0008 text    gold; of Cornucopia, that it had all things necessary for food in it, of Panaces the herb,
p0008 text    that it was good for diseases, of Catholicon the drug, that it is instead of all purges; of
p0008 text    Vulcan’s armor, that it was an armor of proof against all thrusts, and all blows, etc.
p0008 text    Well, that which they falsely or vainly attributed to these things for bodily god, we may
p0008 text    justly and with full measure ascribe unto the Scripture, for spiritual. It is not only an
p0008 text    armor, but also a whole armory of weapons, both offensive and defensive; whereby
p0008 text    we may save ourselves and put the enemy to flight. It is not an herb, but a tree, or
p0008 text    rather a whole paradise of trees of life, which bring forth fruit every month, and the
p0008 text    fruit thereof is for meat, and the leaves for medicine. It is not a pot of Manna, or a
p0008 text    cruse of oil, which were for memory only, or for a meal’s meat or two, but as it were a
p0008 text    shower of heavenly bread sufficient for a whole host, be it never so great; and as it
p0008 text    were a whole cellar full of oil vessels; whereby all our necessities may be provided for,
p0008 text    and our debts discharged. In a word, it is a Panary of wholesome food, against
p0008 text    fenowed traditions; a Physician’s shop (Saint Basil called it) [S. Basil in Psal. primum.]
p0008 text    of preservatives against poisoned heresies; a Pandect of profitable laws, against
p0008 text    rebellious spirits; a treasury of most costly jewels, against beggarly rudiments; finally
p0008 text    a fountain of most pure water springing up unto everlasting life. And what marvel?
p0008 text    The original thereof being from heaven, not from earth; the author being God, not
p0008 text    man; the inditer, the holy spirit, not the wit of the Apostles or Prophets; the Penmen
p0008 text    such as were sanctified from the womb, and endued with a principal portion of God’s
p0008 text    spirit; the matter, verity, piety, purity, uprightness; the form, God’s word, God’s
p0008 text    testimony, God’s oracles, the word of truth, the word of salvation, etc.; the effects, light
p0008 text    of understanding, stableness of persuasion, repentance from dead works, newness of
p0008 text    life, holiness, peace, joy in the holy Ghost; lastly, the end and reward of the study
p0008 text    thereof, fellowship with the Saints, participation of the heavenly nature, fruition of an
p0008 text    inheritance immortal, undefiled, and that never shall fade away: Happy is the man
p0008 text    that delighted in the Scripture, and thrice happy that meditateth in it day and night.
p0008 text    {TRANSLATION NECESSARY}
p0008 text    But how shall men meditate in that, which they cannot understand? How shall they
p0008 text    understand that which is kept close in an unknown tongue? as it is written, “Except I
p0008 text    know the power of the voice, I shall be to him that speaketh, a Barbarian, and he that
p0008 text    speaketh, shall be a Barbarian to me.” [1 Cor 14] The Apostle excepteth no tongue; not
p0008 text    Hebrew the ancientest, not Greek the most copious, not Latin the finest. Nature taught
p0008 text    a natural man to confess, that all of us in those tongues which we do not understand,
p0008 text    are plainly deaf; we may turn the deaf ear unto them. The Scythian counted the
p0008 text    Athenian, whom he did not understand, barbarous; [Clem. Alex. 1 Strom.] so the
p0008 text    Roman did the Syrian, and the Jew (even S. Jerome himself called the Hebrew tongue
p0008 text    barbarous, belike because it was strange to so many) [S. Jerome. Damaso.] so the
p0009 head    5
p0009 text    Emperor of Constantinople [Michael, Theophili fil.] calleth the Latin tongue,
p0009 text    barbarous, though Pope Nicolas do storm at it: [2::Tom. Concil. ex edit. Petri Crab] so
p0009 text    the Jews long before Christ called all other nations, Lognazim, which is little better
p0009 text    than barbarous. Therefore as one complaineth, that always in the Senate of Rome,
p0009 text    there was one or other that called for an interpreter: [Cicero 5::de finibus.] so lest the
p0009 text    Church be driven to the like exigent, it is necessary to have translations in a readiness.
p0009 text    Translation it is that openeth the window, to let in the light; that breaketh the shell,
p0009 text    that we may eat the kernel; that putteth aside the curtain, that we may look into the
p0009 text    most Holy place; that removeth the cover of the well, that we may come by the water,
p0009 text    even as Jacob rolled away the stone from the mouth of the well, by which means the
p0009 text    flocks of Laban were watered [Gen 29:10]. Indeed without translation into the vulgar
p0009 text    tongue, the unlearned are but like children at Jacob’s well (which is deep) [John 4:11]
p0009 text    without a bucket or something to draw with; or as that person mentioned by Isaiah, to
p0009 text    whom when a sealed book was delivered, with this motion, “Read this, I pray thee,” he
p0009 text    was fain to make this answer, “I cannot, for it is sealed.” [Isa 29:11]
p0009 text    {THE TRANSLATION OF THE OLD TESTAMENT OUT OF THE HEBREW INTO GREEK}
p0009 text    While God would be known only in Jacob, and have his Name great in Israel, and in
p0009 text    none other place, while the dew lay on Gideon’s fleece only, and all the earth besides
p0009 text    was dry; then for one and the same people, which spake all of them the language of
p0009 text    Canaan, that is, Hebrew, one and the same original in Hebrew was sufficient. [S.
p0009 text    August. lib 12 contra Faust c32] But, when the fulness of time drew near, that the Sun
p0009 text    of righteousness, the Son of God should come into the world, whom God ordained to
p0009 text    be a reconciliation through faith in his blood, not of the Jew only, but also of the Greek,
p0009 text    yea, of all them that were scattered abroad; then lo, it pleased the Lord to stir up the
p0009 text    spirit of a Greek Prince (Greek for descent and language) even of Ptolemy Philadelph
p0009 text    King of Egypt, to procure the translating of the Book of God out of Hebrew into Greek.
p0009 text    This is the translation of the Seventy Interpreters, commonly so called, which
p0009 text    prepared the way for our Saviour among the Gentiles by written preaching, as Saint
p0009 text    John Baptist did among the Jews by vocal. For the Grecians being desirous of learning,
p0009 text    were not wont to suffer books of worth to lie moulding in Kings’ libraries, but had
p0009 text    many of their servants, ready scribes, to copy them out, and so they were dispersed
p0009 text    and made common. Again, the Greek tongue was well known and made familiar to
p0009 text    most inhabitants in Asia, by reason of the conquest that there the Grecians had made,
p0009 text    as also by the Colonies, which thither they had sent. For the same causes also it was
p0009 text    well understood in many places of Europe, yea, and of Africa too. Therefore the word
p0009 text    of God being set forth in Greek, becometh hereby like a candle set upon a candlestick,
p0009 text    which giveth light to all that are in the house, or like a proclamation sounded forth in
p0009 text    the market place, which most men presently take knowledge of; and therefore that
p0009 text    language was fittest to contain the Scriptures, both for the first Preachers of the Gospel
p0009 text    to appeal unto for witness, and for the learners also of those times to make search and
p0009 text    trial by. It is certain, that that Translation was not so sound and so perfect, but it
p0009 text    needed in many places correction; and who had been so sufficient for this work as the
p0009 text    Apostles or Apostolic men? Yet it seemed good to the holy Ghost and to them, to take
p0009 text    that which they found, (the same being for the greatest part true and sufficient) rather
p0009 text    than making a new, in that new world and green age of the Church, to expose
p0009 text    themselves to many exceptions and cavillations, as though they made a Translations
p0009 text    to serve their own turn, and therefore bearing a witness to themselves, their witness
p0009 text    not to be regarded. This may be supposed to be some cause, why the Translation of the
p0009 text    Seventy was allowed to pass for current. Notwithstanding, though it was commended
p0009 text    generally, yet it did not fully content the learned, no not of the Jews. For not long after
p0010 head    6
p0010 text    Christ, Aquila fell in hand with a new Translation, and after him Theodotion, and after
p0010 text    him Symmachus; yea, there was a fifth and a sixth edition, the Authors whereof were
p0010 text    not known. [Epiphan. de mensur. et ponderibus.] These with the Seventy made up the
p0010 text    Hexapla and were worthily and to great purpose compiled together by Origen.
p0010 text    Howbeit the Edition of the Seventy went away with the credit, and therefore not only
p0010 text    was placed in the midst by Origen (for the worth and excellency thereof above the rest,
p0010 text    as Epiphanius gathered) but also was used by the Greek fathers for the ground and
p0010 text    foundation of their Commentaries. Yea, Epiphanius above named doeth attribute so
p0010 text    much unto it, that he holdeth the Authors thereof not only for Interpreters, but also for
p0010 text    Prophets in some respect [S. August. 2::de dectrin. Christian c. 15]; and Justinian the
p0010 text    Emperor enjoining the Jews his subjects to use especially the Translation of the
p0010 text    Seventy, rendreth this reason thereof, because they were as it were enlightened with
p0010 text    prophetical grace. Yet for all that, as the Egyptians are said of the Prophet to be men
p0010 text    and not God, and their horses flesh and not spirit [Isa 31:3]; so it is evident, (and Saint
p0010 text    Jerome affirmeth as much) [S. Jerome. de optimo genere interpret.] that the Seventy
p0010 text    were Interpreters, they were not Prophets; they did many things well, as learned men;
p0010 text    but yet as men they stumbled and fell, one while through oversight, another while
p0010 text    through ignorance, yea, sometimes they may be noted to add to the Original, and
p0010 text    sometimes to take from it; which made the Apostles to leave them many times, when
p0010 text    they left the Hebrew, and to deliver the sense thereof according to the truth of the
p0010 text    word, as the spirit gave them utterance. This may suffice touching the Greek
p0010 text    Translations of the Old Testament.
p0010 text    {TRANSLATION OUT OF HEBREW AND GREEK INTO LATIN}
p0010 text    There were also within a few hundred years after CHRIST, translations many into
p0010 text    the Latin tongue: for this tongue also was very fit to convey the Law and the Gospel by,
p0010 text    because in those times very many Countries of the West, yea of the South, East and
p0010 text    North, spake or understood Latin, being made Provinces to the Romans. But now the
p0010 text    Latin Translations were too many to be all good, for they were infinite (Latini
p0010 text    Interprets nullo modo numerari possunt, saith S. Augustine.) [S. Augustin. de doctr.
p0010 text    Christ. lib 2 cap II]. Again they were not out of the Hebrew fountain (we speak of the
p0010 text    Latin Translations of the Old Testament) but out of the Greek stream, therefore the
p0010 text    Greek being not altogether clear, the Latin derived from it must needs be muddy. This
p0010 text    moved S. Jerome a most learned father, and the best linguist without controversy, of
p0010 text    his age, or of any that went before him, to undertake the translating of the Old
p0010 text    Testament, out of the very fountain with that evidence of great learning, judgment,
p0010 text    industry, and faithfulness, that he had forever bound the Church unto him, in a debt of
p0010 text    special remembrance and thankfulness.
p0010 text    {THE TRANSLATING OF THE SCRIPTURE INTO THE VULGAR TONGUES}
p0010 text    Now through the Church were thus furnished with Greek and Latin Translations,
p0010 text    even before the faith of CHRIST was generally embraced in the Empire; (for the
p0010 text    learned know that even in S. Jerome’s time, the Consul of Rome and his wife were both
p0010 text    Ethnics, and about the same time the greatest part of the Senate also) [S. Jerome.
p0010 text    Marcell.Zosim] yet for all that the godly-learned were not content to have the
p0010 text    Scriptures in the Language which they themselves understood, Greek and Latin, (as
p0010 text    the good Lepers were not content to fare well themselves, but acquainted their
p0010 text    neighbors with the store that God had sent, that they also might provide for
p0010 text    themselves) [2 Kings 7:9] but also for the behoof and edifying of the unlearned which
p0010 text    hungered and thirsted after righteousness, and had souls to be saved as well as they,
p0010 text    they provided Translations into the vulgar for their Countrymen, insomuch that most
p0010 text    nations under heaven did shortly after their conversion, hear CHRIST speaking unto
p0011 head    7
p0011 text    them in their mother tongue, not by the voice of their Minister only, but also by the
p0011 text    written word translated. If any doubt hereof, he may be satisfied by examples enough,
p0011 text    if enough will serve the turn. First S. Jerome saith, Multarum gentium linguis
p0011 text    Scriptura ante translata, docet falsa esse quae addita sunt, etc. i.e. “The Scripture
p0011 text    being translated before in the languages of many Nations, doth show that those things
p0011 text    that were added (by Lucian and Hesychius) are false.” [S. Jerome. praef. in 4::Evangel.]
p0011 text    So S. Jerome in that place. The same Jerome elsewhere affirmeth that he, the time was,
p0011 text    had set forth the translation of the Seventy suae linguae hominibus, i.e., for his
p0011 text    countrymen of Dalmatia [S. Jerome. Sophronio.] Which words not only Erasmus doth
p0011 text    understand to purport, that S. Jerome translated the Scripture into the Dalmatian
p0011 text    tongue, but also Sixtus Senensis [Six. Sen. lib 4], and Alphonsus à Castro [Alphon. lb 1
p0011 text    ca 23] (that we speak of no more) men not to be excepted against by them of Rome, do
p0011 text    ingenuously confess as much. So, S. Chrysostom that lived in S. Jerome’s time, giveth
p0011 text    evidence with him: “The doctrine of S. John [saith he] did not in such sort [as the
p0011 text    Philosophers’ did] vanish away: but the Syrians, Egyptians, Indians, Persians,
p0011 text    Ethiopians, and infinite other nations being barbarous people translated it into their
p0011 text    [mother] tongue, and have learned to be [true] Philosophers,” he meaneth Christians.
p0011 text    [S. Chrysost. in Johan. cap.I. hom.I.] To this may be added Theodoret, as next unto him,
p0011 text    both for antiquity, and for learning. His words be these, “Every Country that is under
p0011 text    the Sun, is full of these words (of the Apostles and Prophets) and the Hebrew tongue
p0011 text    [he meaneth the Scriptures in the Hebrew tongue] is turned not only into the Language
p0011 text    of the Grecians, but also of the Romans, and Egyptians, and Persians, and Indians, and
p0011 text    Armenians, and Scythians, and Sauromatians, and briefly into all the Languages that
p0011 text    any Nation useth. [Theodor. 5. Therapeut.] So he. In like manner, Ulfilas is reported by
p0011 text    Paulus Diaconus and Isidor (and before them by Sozomen) to have translated the
p0011 text    Scriptures into the Gothic tongue: [P. Diacon. li. 12.] John Bishop of Sevil by Vasseus, to
p0011 text    have turned them into Arabic, about the year of our Lord 717; [Vaseus in Chron.
p0011 text    Hispan.] Bede by Cistertiensis, to have turned a great part of them into Saxon: Efnard
p0011 text    by Trithemius, to have abridged the French Psalter, as Beded had done the Hebrew,
p0011 text    about the year 800: King Alfred by the said Cistertiensis, to have turned the Psalter
p0011 text    into Saxon: [Polydor. Virg. 5 histor.] Methodius by Aventinus (printed at Ingolstadt) to
p0011 text    have turned the Scriptures into Slavonian: [Aventin. lib. 4.] Valdo, Bishop of Frising by
p0011 text    Beatus Rhenanus, to have caused about that time, the Gospels to be translated into
p0011 text    Dutch rhythm, yet extant in the Library of Corbinian: [Circa annum 900. B. Rhenan.
p0011 text    rerum German. lib 2.] Valdus, by divers to have turned them himself into French,
p0011 text    about the year 1160: Charles the Fifth of that name, surnamed the Wise, to have
p0011 text    caused them to be turned into French, about 200 years after Valdus his time, of which
p0011 text    translation there be many copies yet extant, as witnesseth Beroaldus. Much about that
p0011 text    time, even in our King Richard the second’s days, John Trevisa translated them into
p0011 text    English, and many English Bibles in written hand are yet to be seen with divers,
p0011 text    translated as it is very probable, in that age. So the Syrian translation of the New
p0011 text    Testament is in most learned men’s Libraries, of Widminstadius his setting forth, and
p0011 text    the Psalter in Arabic is with many, of Augustinus Nebiensis’ setting forth. So Postel
p0011 text    affirmeth, that in his travel he saw the Gospels in the Ethiopian tongue; And Ambrose
p0011 text    Thesius allegeth the Pslater of the Indians, which he testifieth to have been set forth by
p0011 text    Potken in Syrian characters. So that, to have the Scriptures in the mother tongue is not
p0011 text    a quaint conceit lately taken up, either by the Lord Cromwell in England, [Thuan.] or
p0011 text    by the Lord Radevile in Polony, or by the Lord Ungnadius in the Emperor’s dominion,
p0011 text    but hath been thought upon, and put in practice of old, even from the first times of the
p0011 text    conversion of any Nation; no doubt, because it was esteemed most profitable, to cause
p0012 head    8
p0012 text    faith to grow in men’s hearts the sooner, and to make them to be able to say with the
p0012 text    words of the Psalms, “As we have heard, so we have seen.” [Ps 48:8]
p0012 text    {THE UNWILLINGNESS OF OUR CHIEF ADVERSARIES, THAT THE SCRIPTURES SHOULD}
p0012 text    {BE DIVULGED IN THE MOTHER TONGUE, ETC.}
p0012 text    Now the Church of Rome would seem at the length to bear a motherly affection
p0012 text    towards her children, and to allow them the Scriptures in their mother tongue: but
p0012 text    indeed it is a gift, not deserving to be called a gift, an unprofitable gift: [Sophecles] they
p0012 text    must first get a licence in writing before they may use them, and to get that, they must
p0012 text    approve themselves to their Confessor, that is, to be such as are, if not frozen in the
p0012 text    dregs, yet soured with the leaven of their superstition. Howbeit, it seemed too much to
p0012 text    Clement the Eighth that there should be any Licence granted to have them in the
p0012 text    vulgar tongue, and therefore he overruleth and frustrateth the grant of Pius the
p0012 text    Fourth. [See the observation (set forth by Clemen. His authority) upon the 4. rule of
p0012 text    Pius the 4. his making in the index, lib. prohib. pag. 15. ver. 5.] So much are they afraid
p0012 text    of the light of the Scripture, (Lucifugae Scripturarum, as Tertulian speaketh) that they
p0012 text    will not trust the people with it, no not as it is set forth by their own sworn men, no not
p0012 text    with the Licence of their own Bishops and Inquisitors. Yea, so unwilling they are to
p0012 text    communicate the Scriptures to the people’s understanding in any sort, that they are
p0012 text    not ashamed to confess, that we forced them to translate it into English against their
p0012 text    wills. This seemeth to argue a bad cause, or a bad conscience, or both. Sure we are,
p0012 text    that it is not he that hath good gold, that is afraid to bring it to the touchstone, but he
p0012 text    that hath the counterfeit; [Tertul. de resur. carnis.] neither is it the true man that
p0012 text    shunneth the light, but the malefactor, lest his deeds should be reproved [John 3:20]:
p0012 text    neither is it the plaindealing Merchant that is unwilling to have the weights, or the
p0012 text    meteyard brought in place, but he that useth deceit. But we will let them alone for this
p0012 text    fault, and return to translation.
p0012 text    {THE SPEECHES AND REASONS, BOTH OF OUR BRETHREN, AND OF OUR ADVERSARIES}
p0012 text    {AGAINST THIS WORK}
p0012 text    Many men’s mouths have been open a good while (and yet are not stopped) with
p0012 text    speeches about the Translation so long in hand, or rather perusals of Translations
p0012 text    made before: and ask what may be the reason, what the necessity of the employment:
p0012 text    Hath the Church been deceived, say they, all this while? Hath her sweet bread been
p0012 text    mingled with leaven, her silver with dross, her wine with water, her milk with lime?
p0012 text    (Lacte gypsum male miscetur, saith S. Ireney,) [S. Iren. 3. lib. cap. 19.] We hoped that
p0012 text    we had been in the right way, that we had the Oracles of God delivered unto us, and
p0012 text    that though all the world had cause to be offended and to complain, yet that we had
p0012 text    none. Hath the nurse holden out the breast, and nothing but wind in it? Hath the
p0012 text    bread been delivered by the fathers of the Church, and the same proved to be
p0012 text    lapidosus, as Seneca speaketh? What is it to handle the word of God deceitfully, if this
p0012 text    be not? Thus certain brethren. Also the adversaries of Judah and Jerusalem, like
p0012 text    Sanballat in Nehemiah, mock, as we hear, both the work and the workmen, saying;
p0012 text    “What do these weak Jews, etc. will they make the stones whole again out of the heaps
p0012 text    of dust which are burnt? although they build, yet if a fox go up, he shall even break
p0012 text    down their stony wall.” [Neh 4:3] Was their Translation good before? Why do they
p0012 text    now mend it? Was it not good? Why then was it obtruded to the people? Yea, why did
p0012 text    the Catholics (meaning Popish Romanists) always go in jeopardy, for refusing to go to
p0012 text    hear it? Nay, if it must be translated into English, Catholics are fittest to do it. They
p0012 text    have learning, and they know when a thing is well, they can manum de tabula. We will
p0012 text    answer them both briefly: and the former, being brethren, thus, with S. Jerome,
p0012 text    “Damnamus veteres? Mineme, sed post priorum studia in domo Domini quod
p0013 head    9
p0013 text    possums laboramus.” [S. Jerome. Apolog. advers. Ruffin.] That is, “Do we condemn the
p0013 text    ancient? In no case: but after the endeavors of them that were before us, we take the
p0013 text    best pains we can in the house of God.” As if he said, Being provoked by the example of
p0013 text    the learned men that lived before my time, I have thought it my duty, to assay whether
p0013 text    my talent in the knowledge of the tongues, may be profitable in any measure to God’s
p0013 text    Church, lest I should seem to laboured in them in vain, and lest I should be thought to
p0013 text    glory in men, (although ancient,) above that which was in them. Thus S. Jerome may
p0013 text    be thought to speak.
p0013 text    {A SATISFACTION TO OUR BRETHREN}
p0013 text    And to the same effect say we, that we are so far off from condemning any of their
p0013 text    labors that travailed before us in this kind, either in this land or beyond sea, either in
p0013 text    King Henry’s time, or King Edward’s (if there were any translation, or correction of a
p0013 text    translation in his time) or Queen Elizabeth’s of ever renowned memory, that we
p0013 text    acknowledge them to have been raised up of God, for the building and furnishing of
p0013 text    his Church, and that they deserve to be had of us and of posterity in everlasting
p0013 text    remembrance. The judgment of Aristotle is worthy and well known: “If Timotheus
p0013 text    had not been, we had not had much sweet music; but if Phrynis [Timotheus his
p0013 text    master] had not been, we had not had Timotheus.” Therefore blessed be they, and
p0013 text    most honoured be their name, that break the ice, and giveth onset upon that which
p0013 text    helpeth forward to the saving of souls. Now what can be more available thereto, than
p0013 text    to deliver God’s book unto God’s people in a tongue which they understand? Since of a
p0013 text    hidden treasure, and of a fountain that is sealed, there is no profit, as Ptolemy
p0013 text    Philadelph wrote to the Rabbins or masters of the Jews, as witnesseth Epiphanius: [S.
p0013 text    Epiphan. loco ante citato.] and as S. Augustine saith; “A man had rather be with his
p0013 text    dog than with a stranger (whose tongue is strange unto him).” [S. Augustin. lib. 19. de
p0013 text    civil. Dei. c. 7.] Yet for all that, as nothing is begun and perfected at the same time, and
p0013 text    the later thoughts are thought to be the wiser: so, if we building upon their foundation
p0013 text    that went before us, and being holpen by their labours, do endeavor to make that
p0013 text    better which they left so good; no man, we are sure, hath cause to mislike us; they, we
p0013 text    persuade ourselves, if they were alive, would thank us. The vintage of Abienzer, that
p0013 text    strake the stroke: yet the gleaning of grapes of Ephraim was not to be despised. See
p0013 text    Judges 8:2. Joash the king of Israel did not satisfy himself, till he had smitten the
p0013 text    ground three times; and yet he offended the Prophet, for giving over then. [2 Kings
p0013 text    13:18-19] Aquila, of whom we spake before, translated the Bible as carefully, and as
p0013 text    skilfully as he could; and yet he thought good to go over it again, and then it got the
p0013 text    credit with the Jews, to be called accurately done, as Saint Jerome witnesseth. [S.
p0013 text    Jerome. in Ezech. cap. 3.] How many books of profane learning have been gone over
p0013 text    again and again, by the same translators, by others? Of one and the same book of
p0013 text    Aristotle’s Ethics, there are extant not so few as six or seven several translations. Now
p0013 text    if this cost may be bestowed upon the gourd, which affordeth us a little shade, and
p0013 text    which today flourisheth, but tomorrow is cut down; what may we bestow, nay what
p0013 text    ought we not to bestow upon the Vine, the fruit whereof maketh glad the conscience of
p0013 text    man, and the stem whereof abideth forever? And this is the word of God, which we
p0013 text    translate. “What is the chaff to the wheat, saith the Lord?” [Jer 23:28] Tanti vitreum,
p0013 text    quanti verum margaritum (saith Tertullian,) [Tertul. ad Martyr.] if a toy of glass be of
p0013 text    that reckoning with us, how ought we to value the true pearl? [Jerome. ad Salvin.]
p0013 text    Therefore let no man’s eye be evil, because his Majesty’s is good; neither let any be
p0013 text    grieved, that we have a Prince that seeketh the increase of the spiritual wealth of Israel
p0013 text    (let Sanballats and Tobiahs do so, which therefore do bear their just reproof ) but let us
p0013 text    rather bless God from the ground of our heart, for working this religious care in him,
p0014 head    10
p0014 text    to have the translations of the Bible maturely considered of and examined. For by this
p0014 text    means it cometh to pass, that whatsoever is sound already (and all is sound for
p0014 text    substance, in one or other of our editions, and the worst of ours far better than their
p0014 text    authentic vulgar) the same will shine as gold more brightly, being rubbed and
p0014 text    polished; also, if anything be halting, or superfluous, or not so agreeable to the
p0014 text    original, the same may be corrected, and the truth set in place. And what can the King
p0014 text    command to be done, that will bring him more true honour than this? and wherein
p0014 text    could they that have been set a work, approve their duty to the King, yea their
p0014 text    obedience to God, and love to his Saints more, than by yielding their service, and all
p0014 text    that is within them, for the furnishing of the work? But besides all this, they were the
p0014 text    principal motives of it, and therefore ought least to quarrel it: for the very Historical
p0014 text    truth is, that upon the importunate petitions of the Puritans, at his Majesty’s coming to
p0014 text    this Crown, the Conference at Hampton Court having been appointed for hearing their
p0014 text    complaints: when by force of reason they were put from other grounds, they had
p0014 text    recourse at the last, to this shift, that they could not with good conscience subscribe to
p0014 text    the Communion book, since it maintained the Bible as it was there translated, which
p0014 text    was as they said, a most corrupted translation. And although this was judged to be but
p0014 text    a very poor and empty shift; yet even hereupon did his Majesty begin to bethink
p0014 text    himself of the good that might ensue by a new translation, and presently after gave
p0014 text    order for this Translation which is now presented unto thee. Thus much to satisfy our
p0014 text    scrupulous Brethren.
p0014 text    {AN ANSWER TO THE IMPUTATIONS OF OUR ADVERSARIES}
p0014 text    Now to the latter we answer; that we do not deny, nay we affirm and avow, that the
p0014 text    very meanest translation of the Bible in English, set forth by men of our profession,
p0014 text    (for we have seen none of theirs of the whole Bible as yet) containeth the word of God,
p0014 text    nay, is the word of God. As the King’s speech, which he uttereth in Parliament, being
p0014 text    translated into French, Dutch, Italian, and Latin, is still the King’s speech, though it be
p0014 text    not interpreted by every Translator with the like grace, nor peradventure so fitly for
p0014 text    phrase, nor so expressly for sense, everywhere. For it is confessed, that things are to
p0014 text    take their denomination of the greater part; and a natural man could say, Verum ubi
p0014 text    multa nitent in carmine, non ego paucis offendor maculis, etc. [Horace.] A man may
p0014 text    be counted a virtuous man, though he have made many slips in his life, (else, there
p0014 text    were none virtuous, for in many things we offend all) [James 3:2] also a comely man
p0014 text    and lovely, though he have some warts upon his hand, yea, not only freckles upon his
p0014 text    face, but also scars. No cause therefore why the word translated should be denied to
p0014 text    be the word, or forbidden to be current, notwithstanding that some imperfections and
p0014 text    blemishes may be noted in the setting forth of it. For whatever was perfect under the
p0014 text    Sun, where Apostles or Apostolic men, that is, men endued with an extraordinary
p0014 text    measure of God’s spirit, and privileged with the privilege of infallibility, had not their
p0014 text    hand? The Romanists therefore in refusing to hear, and daring to burn the Word
p0014 text    translated, did no less than despite the spirit of grace, from whom originally it
p0014 text    proceeded, and whose sense and meaning, as well as man’s weakness would enable, it
p0014 text    did express. Judge by an example or two. Plutarch writeth, that after that Rome had
p0014 text    been burnt by the Gauls, they fell soon to build it again: but doing it in haste, they did
p0014 text    not cast the streets, nor proportion the houses in such comely fashion, as had been
p0014 text    most slightly and convenient; [Plutarch in Camillo.] was Catiline therefore an honest
p0014 text    man, or a good patriot, that sought to bring it to a combustion? or Nero a good Prince,
p0014 text    that did indeed set it on fire? So, by the story of Ezra, and the prophecy of Haggai it
p0014 text    may be gathered, that the Temple built by Zerubbabel after the return from Babylon,
p0014 text    was by no means to be compared to the former built by Solomon (for they that
p0015 head    11
p0015 text    remembered the former, wept when they considered the latter) [Ezra 3:12]
p0015 text    notwithstanding, might this latter either have been abhorred and forsaken by the
p0015 text    Jews, or profaned by the Greeks? The like we are to think of Translations. The
p0015 text    translation of the Seventy dissenteth from the Original in many places, neither doth it
p0015 text    come near it, for perspicuity, gravity, majesty; yet which of the Apostles did condemn
p0015 text    it? Condemn it? Nay, they used it, (as it is apparent, and as Saint Jerome and most
p0015 text    learned men do confess) which they would not have done, nor by their example of
p0015 text    using it, so grace and commend it to the Church, if it had been unworthy of the
p0015 text    appellation and name of the word of God. And whereas they urge for their second
p0015 text    defence of their vilifying and abusing of the English Bibles, or some pieces thereof,
p0015 text    which they meet with, for that heretics (forsooth) were the Authors of the translations,
p0015 text    (heretics they call us by the same right that they call themselves Catholics, both being
p0015 text    wrong) we marvel what divinity taught them so. We are sure Tertullian was of
p0015 text    another mind: Ex personis probamus fidem, an ex fide personas? [Tertul. de
p0015 text    praescript. contra haereses.] Do we try men’s faith by their persons? we should try
p0015 text    their persons by their faith. Also S. Augustine was of another mind: for he lighting
p0015 text    upon certain rules made by Tychonius a Donatist, for the better understanding of the
p0015 text    word, was not ashamed to make use of them, yea, to insert them into his own book,
p0015 text    with giving commendation to them so far forth as they were worthy to be commended,
p0015 text    as is to be seen in S. Augustine’s third book De doctrina Christiana. [S. August. 3. de
p0015 text    doct. Christ. cap. 30.] To be short, Origen, and the whole Church of God for certain
p0015 text    hundred years, were of another mind: for they were so far from treading under foot,
p0015 text    (much more from burning) the Translation of Aquila a Proselyte, that is, one that had
p0015 text    turned Jew; of Symmachus, and Theodotion, both Ebionites, that is, most vile heretics,
p0015 text    that they joined together with the Hebrew Original, and the Translation of the Seventy
p0015 text    (as hath been before signified out of Epiphanius) and set them forth openly to be
p0015 text    considered of and perused by all. But we weary the unlearned, who need not know so
p0015 text    much, and trouble the learned, who know it already.
p0015 text    Yet before we end, we must answer a third cavil and objection of theirs against us,
p0015 text    for altering and amending our Translations so oft; wherein truly they deal hardly, and
p0015 text    strangely with us. For to whomever was it imputed for a fault (by such as were wise) to
p0015 text    go over that which he had done, and to amend it where he saw cause? Saint Augustine
p0015 text    was not afraid to exhort S. Jerome to a Palinodia or recantation; [S. Aug. Epist. 9.] and
p0015 text    doth even glory that he seeth his infirmities. [S. Aug. Epist. 8.] If we be sons of the
p0015 text    Truth, we must consider what it speaketh, and trample upon our own credit, yea, and
p0015 text    upon other men’s too, if either be any way an hindrance to it. This to the cause: then to
p0015 text    the persons we say, that of all men they ought to be most silent in this case. For what
p0015 text    varieties have they, and what alterations have they made, not only of their Service
p0015 text    books, Portesses and Breviaries, but also of their Latin Translation? The Service book
p0015 text    supposed to be made by S. Ambrose (Officium Ambrosianum) was a great while in
p0015 text    special use and request; but Pope Hadrian calling a Council with the aid of Charles the
p0015 text    Emperor, abolished it, yea, burnt it, and commanded the Service book of Saint Gregory
p0015 text    universally to be used. [Durand. lib. 5. cap. 2.] Well, Officium Gregorianum gets by
p0015 text    this means to be in credit, but doth it continue without change or altering? No, the
p0015 text    very Roman Service was of two fashions, the New fashion, and the Old, (the one used
p0015 text    in one Church, the other in another) as is to be seen in Pamelius a Romanist, his
p0015 text    Preface, before Micrologus. the same Pamelius reporteth out Radulphus de Rivo, that
p0015 text    about the year of our Lord, 1277, Pope Nicolas the Third removed out of the Churches
p0015 text    of Rome, the more ancient books (of Service) and brought into use the Missals of the
p0015 text    Friers Minorites, and commanded them to be observed there; insomuch that about an
p0016 head    12
p0016 text    hundred years after, when the above name Radulphus happened to be at Rome, he
p0016 text    found all the books to be new, (of the new stamp). Neither were there this chopping
p0016 text    and changing in the more ancient times only, but also of late: Pius Quintus himself
p0016 text    confesseth, that every Bishopric almost had a peculiar kind of service, most unlike to
p0016 text    that which others had: which moved him to abolish all other Breviaries, though never
p0016 text    so ancient, and privileged and published by Bishops in their Dioceses, and to establish
p0016 text    and ratify that only which was of his own setting forth, in the year 1568. Now when
p0016 text    the father of their Church, who gladly would heal the sore of the daughter of his
p0016 text    people softly and slightly, and make the best of it, findeth so great fault with them for
p0016 text    their odds and jarring; we hope the children have no great cause to vaunt of their
p0016 text    uniformity. But the difference that appeareth between our Translations, and our often
p0016 text    correcting of them, is the thing that we are specially charged with; let us see therefore
p0016 text    whether they themselves be without fault this way, (if it be to be counted a fault, to
p0016 text    correct) and whether they be fit men to throw stones at us: O tandem maior parcas
p0016 text    insane minori: they that are less sound themselves, out not to object infirmities to
p0016 text    others. [Horat.] If we should tell them that Valla, Stapulensis, Erasmus, and Vives
p0016 text    found fault with their vulgar Translation, and consequently wished the same to be
p0016 text    mended, or a new one to be made, they would answer peradventure, that we
p0016 text    produced their enemies for witnesses against them; albeit, they were in no other sort
p0016 text    enemies, than as S. Paul was to the Galatians, for telling them the truth [Gal 4:16]: and
p0016 text    it were to be wished, that they had dared to tell it them plainlier and oftener. But what
p0016 text    will they say to this, that Pope Leo the Tenth allowed Erasmus’ Translation of the New
p0016 text    Testament, so much different from the vulgar, by his Apostolic Letter and Bull; that the
p0016 text    same Leo exhorted Pagnine to translate the whole Bible, and bare whatsoever charges
p0016 text    was necessary for the work? [Sixtus Senens.] Surely, as the Apostle reasoneth to the
p0016 text    Hebrews, that if the former Law and Testament had been sufficient, there had been no
p0016 text    need of the latter: [Heb 7:11 and 8:7] so we may say, that if the old vulgar had been at
p0016 text    all points allowable, to small purpose had labour and charges been undergone, about
p0016 text    framing of a new. If they say, it was one Pope’s private opinion, and that he consulted
p0016 text    only himself; then we are able to go further with them, and to aver, that more of their
p0016 text    chief men of all sorts, even their own Trent champions Paiva and Vega, and their own
p0016 text    Inquisitors, Hieronymus ab Oleastro, and their own Bishop Isidorus Clarius, and their
p0016 text    own Cardinal Thomas a Vio Caietan, do either make new Translations themselves, or
p0016 text    follow new ones of other men’s making, or note the vulgar Interpreter for halting;
p0016 text    none of them fear to dissent from him, nor yet to except against him. And call they this
p0016 text    an uniform tenor of text and judgment about the text, so many of their Worthies
p0016 text    disclaiming the now received conceit? Nay, we will yet come nearer the quick: doth
p0016 text    not their Paris edition differ from the Lovaine, and Hentenius his from them both, and
p0016 text    yet all of them allowed by authority? Nay, doth not Sixtus Quintus confess, that certain
p0016 text    Catholics (he meaneth certain of his own side) were in such an humor of translating
p0016 text    the Scriptures into Latin, that Satan taking occasion by them, though they thought of
p0016 text    no such matter, did strive what he could, out of so uncertain and manifold a variety of
p0016 text    Translations, so to mingle all things, that nothing might seem to be left certain and
p0016 text    firm in them, etc.? [Sixtus 5. praefat. fixa Bibliis.] Nay, further, did not the same Sixtus
p0016 text    ordain by an inviolable decree, and that with the counsel and consent of his Cardinals,
p0016 text    that the Latin edition of the old and new Testament, which the Council of Trent would
p0016 text    have to be authentic, is the same without controversy which he then set forth, being
p0016 text    diligently corrected and printed in the Printinghouse of Vatican? Thus Sixtus in his
p0016 text    Preface before his Bible. And yet Clement the Eighth his immediate successor,
p0016 text    published another edition of the Bible, containing in it infinite differences from that of
p0017 head    13
p0017 text    Sixtus, (and many of them weighty and material) and yet this must be authentic by all
p0017 text    means. What is to have the faith of our glorious Lord JESUS CHRIST with Yea or Nay, if
p0017 text    this be not? Again, what is sweet harmony and consent, if this be? Therefore, as
p0017 text    Demaratus of Corinth advised a great King, before he talked of the dissensions of the
p0017 text    Grecians, to compose his domestic broils (for at that time his Queen and his son and
p0017 text    heir were at deadly feud with him) so all the while that our adversaries do make so
p0017 text    many and so various editions themselves, and do jar so much about the worth and
p0017 text    authority of them, they can with no show of equity challenge us for changing and
p0017 text    correcting.
p0017 text    {THE PURPOSE OF THE TRANSLATORS, WITH THEIR NUMBER, FURNITURE, CARE, ETC.}
p0017 text    But it is high time to leave them, and to show in brief what we proposed to ourselves,
p0017 text    and what course we held in this our perusal and survey of the Bible. Truly (good
p0017 text    Christian Reader) we never thought from the beginning, that we should need to make
p0017 text    a new Translation, nor yet to make of a bad one a good one, (for then the imputation of
p0017 text    Sixtus had been true in some sort, that our people had been fed with gall of Dragons
p0017 text    instead of wine, with whey instead of milk:) but to make a good one better, or out of
p0017 text    many good ones, one principal good one, not justly to be excepted against; that hath
p0017 text    been our endeavor, that our mark. To that purpose there were many chosen, that were
p0017 text    greater in other men’s eyes than in their own, and that sought the truth rather than
p0017 text    their own praise. Again, they came or were thought to come to the work, not exercendi
p0017 text    causa (as one saith) but exercitati, that is, learned, not to learn: For the chief overseer
p0017 text    and [NOTE: Greek letters omitted] under his Majesty, to whom not only we, but also
p0017 text    our whole Church was much bound, knew by his wisdom, which thing also Nazianzen
p0017 text    taught so long ago, that it is a preposterous order to teach first and to learn after, yea
p0017 text    that [NOTE: Greek letters omitted] to learn and practice together, is neither
p0017 text    commendable for the workman, nor safe for the work. [Idem in Apologet.] Therefore
p0017 text    such were thought upon, as could say modestly with Saint Jerome, Et Hebreaeum
p0017 text    Sermonem ex parte didicimus, et in Latino pene ab ipsis incunabulis etc. detriti sumus.
p0017 text    “Both we have learned the Hebrew tongue in part, and in the Latin we have been
p0017 text    exercised almost from our very cradle.” S. Jerome maketh no mention of the Greek
p0017 text    tongue, wherein yet he did excel, because he translated not the old Testament out of
p0017 text    Greek, but out of Hebrew. And in what sort did these assemble? In the trust of their
p0017 text    own knowledge, or of their sharpness of wit, or deepness of judgment, as it were in an
p0017 text    arm of flesh? At no hand. They trusted in him that hath the key of David, opening and
p0017 text    no man shutting; they prayed to the Lord the Father of our Lord, to the effect that S.
p0017 text    Augustine did; “O let thy Scriptures be my pure delight, let me not be deceived in them,
p0017 text    neither let me deceive by them.” [S. Aug. lib. II. Confess. cap. 2.] In this confidence, and
p0017 text    with this devotion did they assemble together; not too many, lest one should trouble
p0017 text    another; and yet many, lest many things haply might escape them. If you ask what
p0017 text    they had before them, truly it was the Hebrew text of the Old Testament, the Greek of
p0017 text    the New. These are the two golden pipes, or rather conduits, where-through the olive
p0017 text    branches empty themselves into the gold. Saint Augustine calleth them precedent, or
p0017 text    original tongues; [S. August. 3. de doctr. c. 3. etc.] Saint Jerome, fountains. [S. Jerome.
p0017 text    ad Suniam et Fretel.] The same Saint Jerome affirmeth, [S. Jerome. ad Lucinium, Dist.
p0017 text    9 ut veterum.] and Gratian hath not spared to put it into his Decree, That “as the credit
p0017 text    of the old Books” (he meaneth of the Old Testament) “is to be tried by the Hebrew
p0017 text    Volumes, so of the New by the Greek tongue,” he meaneth by the original Greek. If
p0017 text    truth be tried by these tongues, then whence should a Translation be made, but out of
p0017 text    them? These tongues therefore, the Scriptures we say in those tongues, we set before
p0017 text    us to translate, being the tongues wherein God was pleased to speak to his Church by
p0018 head    14
p0018 text    the Prophets and Apostles. Neither did we run over the work with that posting haste
p0018 text    that the Septuagint did, if that be true which is reported of them, that they finished it in
p0018 text    72 days; [Joseph. Antiq. lib. 12.] neither were we barred or hindered from going over
p0018 text    it again, having once done it, like S. Jerome, if that be true which himself reporteth,
p0018 text    that he could no sooner write anything, but presently it was caught from him, and
p0018 text    published, and he could not have leave to mend it: [S. Jerome. ad Pammac. pro libr.
p0018 text    advers. Iovinian.] neither, to be short, were we the first that fell in hand with
p0018 text    translating the Scripture into English, and consequently destitute of former helps, as it
p0018 text    is written of Origen, that he was the first in a manner, that put his hand to write
p0018 text    Commentaries upon the Scriptures, [Sophoc. in Elect.] and therefore no marvel, if he
p0018 text    overshot himself many times. None of these things: the work hath not been huddled
p0018 text    up in 72 days, but hath cost the workmen, as light as it seemeth, the pains of twice
p0018 text    seven times seventy two days and more: matters of such weight and consequence are
p0018 text    to be speeded with maturity: for in a business of movement a man feareth not the
p0018 text    blame of convenient slackness. [S. Chrysost. in II. Thess. cap. 2.] Neither did we think
p0018 text    much to consult the Translators or Commentators, Chaldee, Hebrew, Syrian, Greek or
p0018 text    Latin, no nor the Spanish, French, Italian, or Dutch; neither did we disdain to revise
p0018 text    that which we had done, and to bring back to the anvil that which we had hammered:
p0018 text    but having and using as great helps as were needful, and fearing no reproach for
p0018 text    slowness, nor coveting praise for expedition, we have at length, through the good
p0018 text    hand of the Lord upon us, brought the work to that pass that you see.
p0018 text    {REASONS MOVING US TO SET DIVERSITY OF SENSES IN THE MARGIN, WHERE THERE}
p0018 text    {IS GREAT PROBABILITY FOR EACH}
p0018 text    Some peradventure would have no variety of senses to be set in the margin, lest the
p0018 text    authority of the Scriptures for deciding of controversies by that show of uncertainty,
p0018 text    should somewhat be shaken. But we hold their judgment not to be sound in this point.
p0018 text    For though, “whatsoever things are necessary are manifest,” as S. Chrysostom saith, [S.
p0018 text    Chrysost. in II. Thess. cap. 2.] and as S. Augustine, “In those things that are plainly set
p0018 text    down in the Scriptures, all such matters are found that concern Faith, Hope, and
p0018 text    Charity. [S. Aug. 2. de doctr. Christ. cap. 9.] Yet for all that it cannot be dissembled, that
p0018 text    partly to exercise and whet our wits, partly to wean the curious from the loathing of
p0018 text    them for their everywhere plainness, partly also to stir up our devotion to crave the
p0018 text    assistance of God’s spirit by prayer, and lastly, that we might be forward to seek aid of
p0018 text    our brethren by conference, and never scorn those that be not in all respects so
p0018 text    complete as they should be, being to seek in many things ourselves, it hath pleased
p0018 text    God in his divine providence, here and there to scatter words and sentences of that
p0018 text    difficulty and doubtfulness, not in doctrinal points that concern salvation, (for in such
p0018 text    it hath been vouched that the Scriptures are plain) but in matters of less moment, that
p0018 text    fearfulness would better beseem us than confidence, and if we will resolve upon
p0018 text    modesty with S. Augustine, (though not in this same case altogether, yet upon the same
p0018 text    ground) Melius est debitare de occultis, quam litigare de incertis, [S. Aug li. S. de
p0018 text    Genes. ad liter. cap. 5.] “it is better to make doubt of those things which are secret,
p0018 text    than to strive about those things that are uncertain.” There be many words in the
p0018 text    Scriptures, which be never found there but once, (having neither brother or neighbor,
p0018 text    as the Hebrews speak) so that we cannot be holpen by conference of places. Again,
p0018 text    there be many rare names of certain birds, beasts and precious stones, etc. concerning
p0018 text    the Hebrews themselves are so divided among themselves for judgment, that they
p0018 text    may seem to have defined this or that, rather because they would say something, than
p0018 text    because they were sure of that which they said, as S. Jerome somewhere saith of the
p0018 text    Septuagint. Now in such a case, doth not a margin do well to admonish the Reader to
p0019 head    15
p0019 text    seek further, and not to conclude or dogmatize upon this or that peremptorily? For as
p0019 text    it is a fault of incredulity, to doubt of those things that are evident: so to determine of
p0019 text    such things as the Spirit of God hath left (even in the judgment of the judicious)
p0019 text    questionable, can be no less than presumption. Therefore as S. Augustine saith, that
p0019 text    variety of Translations is profitable for the finding out of the sense of the Scriptures:
p0019 text    [S. Aug. 2. De doctr. Christian. cap. 14.] so diversity of signification and sense in the
p0019 text    margin, where the text is no so clear, must needs do good, yea, is necessary, as we are
p0019 text    persuaded. We know that Sixtus Quintus expressly forbiddeth, that any variety of
p0019 text    readings of their vulgar edition, should be put in the margin, [Sixtus 5. praef. Bibliae.]
p0019 text    (which though it be not altogether the same thing to that we have in hand, yet it
p0019 text    looketh that way) but we think he hath not all of his own side his favorers, for this
p0019 text    conceit. They that are wise, had rather have their judgments at liberty in differences of
p0019 text    readings, than to be captivated to one, when it may be the other. If they were sure that
p0019 text    their high Priest had all laws shut up in his breast, as Paul the Second bragged, [Plat. in
p0019 text    Paulo secundo.] and that he were as free from error by special privilege, as the
p0019 text    Dictators of Rome were made by law inviolable, it were another matter; then his word
p0019 text    were an Oracle, his opinion a decision. But the eyes of the world are now open, God be
p0019 text    thanked, and have been a great while, they find that he is subject to the same
p0019 text    affections and infirmities that others be, that his skin is penetrable, and therefore so
p0019 text    much as he proveth, not as much as he claimeth, they grant and embrace.
p0019 text    {REASONS INDUCING US NOT TO STAND CURIOUSLY UPON AN IDENTITY OF}
p0019 text    {PHRASING}
p0019 text    Another things we think good to admonish thee of (gentle Reader) that we have not
p0019 text    tied ourselves to an uniformity of phrasing, or to an identity of words, as some
p0019 text    peradventure would wish that we had done, because they observe, that some learned
p0019 text    men somewhere, have been as exact as they could that way. Truly, that we might not
p0019 text    vary from the sense of that which we had translated before, if the word signified that
p0019 text    same in both places (for there be some words that be not the same sense everywhere)
p0019 text    we were especially careful, and made a conscience, according to our duty. But, that we
p0019 text    should express the same notion in the same particular word; as for example, if we
p0019 text    translate the Hebrew or Greek word once by PURPOSE, never to call it INTENT; if one
p0019 text    where JOURNEYING, never TRAVELING; if one where THINK, never SUPPOSE; if one
p0019 text    where PAIN, never ACHE; if one where JOY, never GLADNESS, etc. Thus to mince the
p0019 text    matter, we thought to savour more of curiosity than wisdom, and that rather it would
p0019 text    breed scorn in the Atheist, than bring profit to the godly Reader. For is the kingdom of
p0019 text    God to become words or syllables? why should we be in bondage to them if we may be
p0019 text    free, use one precisely when we may use another no less fit, as commodiously? A godly
p0019 text    Father in the Primitive time showed himself greatly moved, that one of
p0019 text    newfangledness called [NOTE: Greek omitted but was a dispute over the word for “a
p0019 text    bed”] [Niceph. Calist. lib.8. cap.42.] though the difference be little or none; and
p0019 text    another reporteth that he was much abused for turning “Cucurbita” (to which reading
p0019 text    the people had been used) into “Hedera”. [S. Jerome in 4. Ionae. See S. Aug: epist. 10.]
p0019 text    Now if this happens in better times, and upon so small occasions, we might justly fear
p0019 text    hard censure, if generally we should make verbal and unnecessary changings. We
p0019 text    might also be charged (by scoffers) with some unequal dealing towards a great
p0019 text    number of good English words. For as it is written of a certain great Philosopher, that
p0019 text    he should say, that those logs were happy that were made images to be worshipped;
p0019 text    for their fellows, as good as they, lay for blocks behind the fire: so if we should say, as it
p0019 text    were, unto certain words, Stand up higher, have a place in the Bible always, and to
p0019 text    others of like quality, Get ye hence, be banished forever, we might be taxed
p0020 head    16
p0020 text    peradventure with S. James his words, namely, “To be partial in ourselves and judges
p0020 text    of evil thoughts.” Add hereunto, that niceness in words was always counted the next
p0020 text    step to trifling, and so was to be curious about names too: also that we cannot follow a
p0020 text    better pattern for elocution than God himself; therefore he using divers words, in his
p0020 text    holy writ, and indifferently for one thing in nature: [see Euseb. li. 12. ex Platon.] we, if
p0020 text    we will not be superstitious, may use the same liberty in our English versions out of
p0020 text    Hebrew and Greek, for that copy or store that he hath given us. Lastly, we have on the
p0020 text    one side avoided the scrupulosity of the Puritans, who leave the old Ecclesiastical
p0020 text    words, and betake them to other, as when they put WASHING for BAPTISM, and
p0020 text    CONGREGATION instead of CHURCH: as also on the other side we have shunned the
p0020 text    obscurity of the Papists, in their AZIMES, TUNIKE, RATIONAL, HOLOCAUSTS,
p0020 text    PRAEPUCE, PASCHE, and a number of such like, whereof their late Translation is full,
p0020 text    and that of purpose to darken the sense, that since they must needs translate the Bible,
p0020 text    yet by the language thereof, it may be kept from being understood. But we desire that
p0020 text    the Scripture may speak like itself, as in the language of Canaan, that it may be
p0020 text    understood even of the very vulgar.
p0020 text    Many other things we might give thee warning of (gentle Reader) if we had not
p0020 text    exceeded the measure of a Preface already. It remaineth, that we commend thee to
p0020 text    God, and to the Spirit of his grace, which is able to build further than we can ask or
p0020 text    think. He removeth the scales from our eyes, the vail from our hearts, opening our
p0020 text    wits that we may understand his word, enlarging our hearts, yea correcting our
p0020 text    affections, that we may love it to the end. Ye are brought unto fountains of living water
p0020 text    which ye digged not; do not cast earth into them with the Philistines, neither prefer
p0020 text    broken pits before them with the wicked Jews. [Gen 26:15. Jer 2:13.] Others have
p0020 text    laboured, and you may enter into their labours; O receive not so great things in vain, O
p0020 text    despise not so great salvation! Be not like swine to tread under foot so precious things,
p0020 text    neither yet like dogs to tear and abuse holy things. Say not to our Saviour with the
p0020 text    Gergesites, Depart out of our coast [Matt 8:34]; neither yet with Esau sell your
p0020 text    birthright for a mess of pottage [Heb 12:16]. If light be come into the world, love not
p0020 text    darkness more than light; if food, if clothing be offered, go not naked, starve not
p0020 text    yourselves. Remember the advice of Nazianzene, “It is a grievous thing” (or
p0020 text    dangerous) “to neglect a great fair, and to seek to make markets afterwards: also the
p0020 text    encouragement of S. Chrysostom, “It is altogether impossible, that he that is sober”
p0020 text    (and watchful) “should at any time be neglected:” [S. Chrysost. in epist. ad Rom. cap.
p0020 text    14. oral. 26.] Lastly, the admonition and menacing of S. Augustine, “They that despise
p0020 text    God’s will inviting them, shall feel God’s will taking vengeance of them.” [S. August. ad
p0020 text    artic. sibi falso object. Artic. 16.] It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living
p0020 text    God; [Heb 10:31] but a blessed thing it is, and will bring us to everlasting blessedness in
p0020 text    the end, when God speaketh unto us, to hearken; when he setteth his word before us,
p0020 text    to read it; when he stretcheth out his hand and calleth, to answer, Here am I, here we
p0020 text    are to do thy will, O God. The Lord work a care and conscience in us to know him and
p0020 text    serve him, that we may be acknowledged of him at the appearing of our Lord Jesus
p0020 text    Christ, to whom with the holy Ghost, be all praise and thanksgiving.
p0020 text    Amen.
