p1173 verse   2 They went through the wilderness that was not inhabited, and pitched tents in
p1173 text    places where there lay no way.
p1174 head    Wisdom 11:3 1170 Wisdom 12:1
p1174 verse   3 They stood against their enemies, and were avenged of their adversaries.
p1174 verse   4When they were thirsty, they called upon thee, and water was given them out of the
p1174 text    flinty rock, and their thirst was quenched out of the hard stone.
p1174 verse   5 For by what things their enemies were punished, by the same they in their need
p1174 text    were benefited.
p1174 verse   6 For instead of a perpetual running river troubled with foul blood,
p1174 verse   7 For a manifest reproof of that commandment, whereby the infants were slain, thou
p1174 text    gavest unto them abundance of water by a means which they hoped not for:
p1174 verse   8 Declaring by that thirst then how thou hadst punished their adversaries.
p1174 verse   9 For when they were tried albeit but in mercy chastised, they knew how the ungodly
p1174 text    were judged in wrath and tormented, thirsting in another manner than the just.
p1174 verse   10 For these thou didst admonish and try, as a father: but the other, as a severe king,
p1174 text    thou didst condemn and punish.
p1174 verse   11 Whether they were absent or present, they were vexed alike.
p1174 verse   12 For a double grief came upon them, and a groaning for the remembrance of things
p1174 text    past.
p1174 verse   13 For when they heard by their own punishments the other to be benefited, they
p1174 text    had some feeling of the Lord.
p1174 verse   14 For whom they respected with scorn, when he was long before thrown out at the
p1174 text    casting forth of the infants, him in the end, when they saw what came to pass, they
p1174 text    admired.
p1174 verse   15 But for the foolish devices of their wickedness, wherewith being deceived they
p1174 text    worshipped serpents void of reason, and vile beasts, thou didst send a multitude of
p1174 text    unreasonable beasts upon them for vengeance;
p1174 verse   16 That they might know, that wherewithal a man sinneth, by the same also shall he
p1174 text    be punished.
p1174 verse   17 For thy Almighty hand, that made the world of matter without form, wanted not
p1174 text    means to send among them a multitude of bears or fierce lions,
p1174 verse   18 Or unknown wild beasts, full of rage, newly created, breathing out either a fiery
p1174 text    vapour, or filthy scents of scattered smoke, or shooting horrible sparkles out of their
p1174 text    eyes:
p1174 verse   19 Whereof not only the harm might dispatch them at once, but also the terrible sight
p1174 text    utterly destroy them.
p1174 verse   20 Yea, and without these might they have fallen down with one blast, being
p1174 text    persecuted of vengeance, and scattered abroad through the breath of thy power: but
p1174 text    thou hast ordered all things in measure and number and weight.
p1174 verse   21 For thou canst shew thy great strength at all times when thou wilt; and who may
p1174 text    withstand the power of thine arm?
p1174 verse   22 For the whole world before thee is as a little grain of the balance, yea, as a drop of
p1174 text    the morning dew that falleth down upon the earth.
p1174 verse   23 But thou hast mercy upon all; for thou canst do all things, and winkest at the sins
p1174 text    of men, because they should amend.
p1174 verse   24 For thou lovest all the things that are, and abhorrest nothing which thou hast
p1174 text    made: for never wouldest thou have made any thing, if thou hadst hated it.
p1174 verse   25 And how could any thing have endured, if it had not been thy will? or been
p1174 text    preserved, if not called by thee?
p1174 verse   26 But thou sparest all: for they are thine, O Lord, thou lover of souls.
p1174 chapter 12
p1174 verse   1 For thine incorruptible Spirit is in all things.
p1175 head    Wisdom 12:2 1171 Wisdom 12:22
p1175 verse   2 Therefore chastenest thou them by little and little that offend, and warnest them by
p1175 text    putting them in remembrance wherein they have offended, that leaving their
p1175 text    wickedness they may believe on thee, O Lord.
p1175 verse   3 For it was thy will to destroy by the hands of our fathers both those old inhabitants
p1175 text    of thy holy land,
p1175 verse   4Whom thou hatedst for doing most odious works of witchcrafts, and wicked
p1175 text    sacrifices;
p1175 verse   5 And also those merciless murderers of children, and devourers of man’s flesh, and
p1175 text    the feasts of blood,
p1175 verse   6 With their priests out of the midst of their idolatrous crew, and the parents, that
p1175 text    killed with their own hands souls destitute of help:
p1175 verse   7 That the land, which thou esteemedst above all other, might receive a worthy
p1175 text    colony of God’s children.
p1175 verse   8 Nevertheless even those thou sparedst as men, and didst send wasps, forerunners
p1175 text    of thine host, to destroy them by little and little.
p1175 verse   9 Not that thou wast unable to bring the ungodly under the hand of the righteous in
p1175 text    battle, or to destroy them at once with cruel beasts, or with one rough word:
p1175 verse   10 But executing thy judgments upon them by little and little, thou gavest them place
p1175 text    of repentance, not being ignorant that they were a naughty generation, and that their
p1175 text    malice was bred in them, and that their cogitation would never be changed.
p1175 verse   11 For it was a cursed seed from the beginning; neither didst thou for fear of any man
p1175 text    give them pardon for those things wherein they sinned.
p1175 verse   12 For who shall say, What hast thou done? or who shall withstand thy judgment? or
p1175 text    who shall accuse thee for the nations that perish, whom thou made? or who shall
p1175 text    come to stand against thee, to be revenged for the unrighteous men?
p1175 verse   13 For neither is there any God but thou that careth for all, to whom thou mightest
p1175 text    shew that thy judgment is not unright.
p1175 verse   14 Neither shall king or tyrant be able to set his face against thee for any whom thou
p1175 text    hast punished.
p1175 verse   15 Forsomuch then as thou art righteous thyself, thou orderest all things righteously:
p1175 text    thinking it not agreeable with thy power to condemn him that hath not deserved to be
p1175 text    punished.
p1175 verse   16 For thy power is the beginning of righteousness, and because thou art the Lord of
p1175 text    all, it maketh thee to be gracious unto all.
p1175 verse   17 For when men will not believe that thou art of a full power, thou shewest thy
p1175 text    strength, and among them that know it thou makest their boldness manifest.
p1175 verse   18 But thou, mastering thy power, judgest with equity, and orderest us with great
p1175 text    favour: for thou mayest use power when thou wilt.
p1175 verse   19 But by such works hast thou taught thy people that the just man should be
p1175 text    merciful, and hast made thy children to be of a good hope that thou givest repentance
p1175 text    for sins.
p1175 verse   20 For if thou didst punish the enemies of thy children, and the condemned to death,
p1175 text    with such deliberation, giving them time and place, whereby they might be delivered
p1175 text    from their malice:
p1175 verse   21 With how great circumspection didst thou judge thine own sons, unto whose
p1175 text    fathers thou hast sworn, and made covenants of good promises?
p1175 verse   22 Therefore, whereas thou dost chasten us, thou scourgest our enemies a thousand
p1175 text    times more, to the intent that, when we judge, we should carefully think of thy
p1175 text    goodness, and when we ourselves are judged, we should look for mercy.
p1176 head    Wisdom 12:23 1172 Wisdom 13:16
p1176 verse   23 Wherefore, whereas men have lived dissolutely and unrighteously, thou hast
p1176 text    tormented them with their own abominations.
p1176 verse   24 For they went astray very far in the ways of error, and held them for gods, which
p1176 text    even among the beasts of their enemies were despised, being deceived, as children of
p1176 text    no understanding.
p1176 verse   25 Therefore unto them, as to children without the use of reason, thou didst send a
p1176 text    judgment to mock them.
p1176 verse   26 But they that would not be reformed by that correction, wherein he dallied with
p1176 text    them, shall feel a judgment worthy of God.
p1176 verse   27 For, look, for what things they grudged, when they were punished, that is, for
p1176 text    them whom they thought to be gods; {now }being punished in them, when they saw it,
p1176 text    they acknowledged him to be the true God, whom before they denied to know: and
p1176 text    therefore came extreme damnation upon them.
p1176 chapter 13
p1176 verse   1 Surely vain are all men by nature, who are ignorant of God, and could not out of
p1176 text    the good things that are seen know him that is: neither by considering the works did
p1176 text    they acknowledge the workmaster;
p1176 verse   2 But deemed either fire, or wind, or the swift air, or the circle of the stars, or the
p1176 text    violent water, or the lights of heaven, to be the gods which govern the world.
p1176 verse   3 With whose beauty if they being delighted took them to be gods; let them know
p1176 text    how much better the Lord of them is: for the first author of beauty hath created them.
p1176 verse   4 But if they were astonished at their power and virtue, let them understand by
p1176 text    them, how much mightier he is that made them.
p1176 verse   5 For by the greatness and beauty of the creatures proportionably the maker of them
p1176 text    is seen.
p1176 verse   6 But yet for this they are the less to be blamed: for they peradventure err, seeking
p1176 text    God, and desirous to find him.
p1176 verse   7 For being conversant in his works they search him diligently, and believe their
p1176 text    sight: because the things are beautiful that are seen.
p1176 verse   8 Howbeit neither are they to be pardoned.
p1176 verse   9 For if they were able to know so much, that they could aim at the world; how did
p1176 text    they not sooner find out the Lord thereof?
p1176 verse   10 But miserable are they, and in dead things is their hope, who call them gods, which
p1176 text    are the works of men’s hands, gold and silver, to shew art in, and resemblances of
p1176 text    beasts, or a stone good for nothing, the work of an ancient hand.
p1176 verse   11 Now a carpenter that felleth timber, after he hath sawn down a tree meet for the
p1176 text    purpose, and taken off all the bark skilfully round about, and hath wrought it
p1176 text    handsomely, and made a vessel thereof fit for the service of man’s life;
p1176 verse   12 And after spending the refuse of his work to dress his meat, hath filled himself;
p1176 verse   13 And taking the very refuse among those which served to no use, being a crooked
p1176 text    piece of wood, and full of knots, hath carved it diligently, when he had nothing else to
p1176 text    do, and formed it by the skill of his understanding, and fashioned it to the image of a
p1176 text    man;
p1176 verse   14 Or made it like some vile beast, laying it over with vermilion, and with paint
p1176 text    colouring it red, and covering every spot therein;
p1176 verse   15 And when he had made a convenient room for it, set it in a wall, and made it fast
p1176 text    with iron:
p1176 verse   16 For he provided for it that it might not fall, knowing that it was unable to help
p1176 text    itself; for it is an image, and hath need of help:
p1177 head    Wisdom 13:17 1173 Wisdom 14:21
p1177 verse   17 Then maketh he prayer for his goods, for his wife and children, and is not
p1177 text    ashamed to speak to that which hath no life.
p1177 verse   18 For health he calleth upon that which is weak: for life prayeth to that which is
p1177 text    dead; for aid humbly beseecheth that which hath least means to help: and for a good
p1177 text    journey he asketh of that which cannot set a foot forward:
p1177 verse   19 And for gaining and getting, and for good success of his hands, asketh ability to do
p1177 text    of him, that is most unable to do any thing.
p1177 chapter 14
p1177 verse   1 Again, one preparing himself to sail, and about to pass through the raging waves,
p1177 text    calleth upon a piece of wood more rotten than the vessel that carrieth him.
p1177 verse   2 For verily desire of gain devised that, and the workman built it by his skill.
p1177 verse   3 But thy providence, O Father, governeth it: for thou hast made a way in the sea, and
p1177 text    a safe path in the waves;
p1177 verse   4 Shewing that thou canst save from all danger: yea, though a man went to sea
p1177 text    without art.
p1177 verse   5 Nevertheless thou wouldest not that the works of thy wisdom should be idle, and
p1177 text    therefore do men commit their lives to a small piece of wood, and passing the rough
p1177 text    sea in a weak vessel are saved.
p1177 verse   6 For in the old time also, when the proud giants perished, the hope of the world
p1177 text    governed by thy hand escaped in a weak vessel, and left to all ages a seed of generation.
p1177 verse   7 For blessed is the wood whereby righteousness cometh.
p1177 verse   8 But that which is made with hands is cursed, as well it, as he that made it: he,
p1177 text    because he made it; and it, because, being corruptible, it was called god.
p1177 verse   9 For the ungodly and his ungodliness are both alike hateful unto God.
p1177 verse   10 For that which is made shall be punished together with him that made it.
p1177 verse   11 Therefore even upon the idols of the Gentiles shall there be a visitation: because
p1177 text    in the creature of God they are become an abomination, and stumblingblocks to the
p1177 text    souls of men, and a snare to the feet of the unwise.
p1177 verse   12 For the devising of idols was the beginning of spiritual fornication, and the
p1177 text    invention of them the corruption of life.
p1177 verse   13 For neither were they from the beginning, neither shall they be for ever.
p1177 verse   14 For by the vain glory of men they entered into the world, and therefore shall they
p1177 text    come shortly to an end.
p1177 verse   15 For a father afflicted with untimely mourning, when he hath made an image of his
p1177 text    child soon taken away, now honoured him as a god, which was then a dead man, and
p1177 text    delivered to those that were under him ceremonies and sacrifices.
p1177 verse   16 Thus in process of time an ungodly custom grown strong was kept as a law, and
p1177 text    graven images were worshipped by the commandments of kings.
p1177 verse   17 Whom men could not honour in presence, because they dwelt far off, they took
p1177 text    the counterfeit of his visage from far, and made an express image of a king whom they
p1177 text    honoured, to the end that by this their forwardness they might flatter him that was
p1177 text    absent, as if he were present.
p1177 verse   18 Also the singular diligence of the artificer did help to set forward the ignorant to
p1177 text    more superstition.
p1177 verse   19 For he, peradventure willing to please one in authority, forced all his skill to make
p1177 text    the resemblance of the best fashion.
p1177 verse   20 And so the multitude, allured by the grace of the work, took him now for a god,
p1177 text    which a little before was but honoured.
p1177 verse   21 And this was an occasion to deceive the world: for men, serving either calamity or
p1177 text    tyranny, did ascribe unto stones and stocks the incommunicable name.

p1178 verse   22 Moreover this was not enough for them, that they erred in the knowledge of God;

p1178 chapter 15
p1178 verse   1 But thou, O God, art gracious and true, longsuffering, and in mercy ordering all
p1178 text    things,
p1178 verse   2 For if we sin, we are thine, knowing thy power: but we will not sin, knowing that
p1178 text    we are counted thine.
p1178 verse   3 For to know thee is perfect righteousness: yea, to know thy power is the root of
p1178 text    immortality.
p1178 verse   4 For neither did the mischievous invention of men deceive us, nor an image spotted
p1178 text    with divers colours, the painter’s fruitless labour;
p1178 verse   5 The sight whereof enticeth fools to lust after it, and so they desire the form of a
p1178 text    dead image, that hath no breath.
p1178 verse   6 Both they that make them, they that desire them, and they that worship them, are
p1178 text    lovers of evil things, and are worthy to have such things to trust upon.
p1178 verse   7 For the potter, tempering soft earth, fashioneth every vessel with much labour for
p1178 text    our service: yea, of the same clay he maketh both the vessels that serve for clean uses,
p1178 text    and likewise also all such as serve to the contrary: but what is the use of either sort, the
p1178 text    potter himself is the judge.
p1178 verse   8 And employing his labours lewdly, he maketh a vain god of the same clay, even he
p1178 text    which a little before was made of earth himself, and within a little while after
p1178 text    returneth to the same, out when his life which was lent him shall be demanded.
p1178 verse   9 Notwithstanding his care is, not that he shall have much labour, nor that his life is
p1178 text    short: but striveth to excel goldsmiths and silversmiths, and endeavoureth to do like
p1178 text    the workers in brass, and counteth it his glory to make counterfeit things.
p1178 verse   10 His heart is ashes, his hope is more vile than earth, and his life of less value than
p1178 text    clay:
p1178 verse   11 Forasmuch as he knew not his Maker, and him that inspired into him an active
p1178 text    soul, and breathed in a living spirit.

p1184 title   The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or
p1184 title   Ecclesiasticus
p1184 text    {A Prologue made by an uncertain Author}
p1184 text    This Jesus was the son of Sirach, and grandchild to Jesus of the same name with him:
p1184 text    this man therefore lived in the latter times, after the people had been led away captive,
p1184 text    and called home a again, and almost after all the prophets. Now his grandfather Jesus,
p1184 text    as he himself witnesseth, was a man of great diligence and wisdom among the
p1184 text    Hebrews, who did not only gather the grave and short sentences of wise men, that had
p1184 text    been before him, but himself also uttered some of his own, full of much understanding
p1184 text    and wisdom. When as therefore the first Jesus died, leaving this book almost
p1184 text    perfected, Sirach his son receiving it after him left it to his own son Jesus, who, having
p1184 text    gotten it into his hands, compiled it all orderly into one volume, and called it Wisdom,
p1184 text    intituling it both by his own name, his father’s name, and his grandfather’s; alluring
p1184 text    the hearer by the very name of Wisdom to have a greater love to the study of this book.
p1184 text    It containeth therefore wise sayings, dark sentences, and parables, and certain
p1184 text    particular ancient godly stories of men that pleased God; also his prayer and song;
p1184 text    moreover, what benefits God had vouchsafed his people, and what plagues he had
p1184 text    heaped upon their enemies. This Jesus did imitate Solomon, and was no less famous
p1184 text    for wisdom and learning, both being indeed a man of great learning, and so reputed
p1184 text    also.
p1184 text    {The Prologue of the Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach.}
p1184 text    Whereas many and great things have been delivered unto us by the law and the
p1184 text    prophets, and by others that have followed their steps, for the which things Israel
p1184 text    ought to be commended for learning and wisdom; and whereof not only the readers
p1184 text    must needs become skilful themselves, but also they that desire to learn be able to
p1184 text    profit them which are without, both by speaking and writing: my grandfather Jesus,
p1184 text    when he had much given himself to the reading of the law, and the prophets, and other
p1184 text    books of our fathers, and had gotten therein good judgment, was drawn on also
p1184 text    himself to write something pertaining to learning and wisdom; to the intent that those
p1184 text    which are desirous to learn, and are addicted to these things, might profit much more
p1184 text    in living according to the law. Wherefore let me intreat you to read it with favour and
p1184 text    attention, and to pardon us, wherein we may seem to come short of some words,
p1184 text    which we have laboured to interpret. For the same things uttered in Hebrew, and
p1184 text    translated into another tongue, have not the same force in them: and not only these
p1184 text    things, but the law itself, and the prophets, and the rest of the books, have no small
p1184 text    difference, when they are spoken in their own language. For in the eight and thirtieth
p1184 text    year coming into Egypt, when Euergetes was king, and continuing there some time, I
p1184 text    found a book of no small learning: therefore I thought it most necessary for me to
p1184 text    bestow some diligence and travail to interpret it; using great watchfulness and skill in
p1184 text    that space to bring the book to an end, and set it forth for them also, which in a strange
p1184 text    country are willing to learn, being prepared before in manners to live after the law.

p1242 verse   1 A copy of an epistle, which Jeremy sent unto them which were to be led captives

p1243 text    them, when ye see the multitude before them and behind them, worshipping them.

p1243 verse   7 For mine angel is with you, and I myself caring for your souls.

p1243 text    and laid over with silver; yet are they but false, and cannot speak.
p1243 verse   9 And taking gold, as it were for a virgin that loveth to go gay, they make crowns for
p1243 text    the heads of their gods.

p1243 text    upon themselves.

p1243 verse   14 And he that cannot put to death one that offendeth him holdeth a sceptre, as
p1243 text    though he were a judge of the country.
p1243 verse   15 He hath also in his right hand a dagger and an ax: but cannot deliver himself from
p1243 text    war and thieves.
p1243 verse   16 Whereby they are known not to be gods: therefore fear them not.

p1243 text    is with their gods: when they be set up in the temple, their eyes be full of dust through
p1243 text    the feet of them that come in.
p1243 verse   18 And as the doors are made sure on every side upon him that offendeth the king, as
p1243 text    being committed to suffer death: even so the priests make fast their temples with

p1243 verse   19 They light them candles, yea, more than for themselves, whereof they cannot see

p1249 verse   1 There dwelt a man in Babylon, called Joacim:
p1249 verse   2 And he took a wife, whose name was Susanna, the daughter of Chelcias, a very fair
p1249 text    woman, and one that feared the Lord.
p1249 verse   3 Her parents also were righteous, and taught their daughter according to the law of
p1249 text    Moses.
p1249 verse   4 Now Joacim was a great rich man, and had a fair garden joining unto his house:
p1249 text    and to him resorted the Jews; because he was more honourable than all others.
p1249 verse   5 The same year were appointed two of the ancients of the people to be judges, such
p1249 text    as the Lord spake of, that wickedness came from Babylon from ancient judges, who
p1249 text    seemed to govern the people.
p1249 verse   6 These kept much at Joacim’s house: and all that had any suits in law came unto
p1249 text    them.
p1249 verse   7 Now when the people departed away at noon, Susanna went into her husband’s
p1249 text    garden to walk.
p1249 verse   8 And the two elders saw her going in every day, and walking; so that their lust was
p1249 text    inflamed toward her.
p1249 verse   9 And they perverted their own mind, and turned away their eyes, that they might
p1249 text    not look unto heaven, nor remember just judgments.
p1249 verse   10 And albeit they both were wounded with her love, yet durst not one shew another
p1249 text    his grief.
p1249 verse   11 For they were ashamed to declare their lust, that they desired to have to do with
p1249 text    her.
p1249 verse   12 Yet they watched diligently from day to day to see her.
p1249 verse   13 And the one said to the other, Let us now go home: for it is dinner time.
p1249 verse   14 So when they were gone out, they parted the one from the other, and turning back
p1249 text    again they came to the same place; and after that they had asked one another the
p1249 text    cause, they acknowledged their lust: then appointed they a time both together, when
p1249 text    they might find her alone.
p1249 verse   15 And it fell out, as they watched a fit time, she went in as before with two maids
p1249 text    only, and she was desirous to wash herself in the garden: for it was hot.
p1249 verse   16 And there was no body there save the two elders, that had hid themselves, and
p1249 text    watched her.
p1249 verse   17 Then she said to her maids, Bring me oil and washing balls, and shut the garden
p1249 text    doors, that I may wash me.

p1323 verse   1 And Josias held the feast of the passover in Jerusalem unto his Lord, and offered
p1323 text    the passover the fourteenth day of the first month;
p1323 verse   2 Having set the priests according to their daily courses, being arrayed in long
p1323 text    garments, in the temple of the Lord.
p1323 verse   3 And he spake unto the Levites, the holy ministers of Israel, that they should hallow
p1323 text    themselves unto the Lord, to set the holy ark of the Lord in the house that king
p1323 text    Solomon the son of David had built:
p1323 verse   4 And said, Ye shall no more bear the ark upon your shoulders: now therefore serve
p1323 text    the Lord your God, and minister unto his people Israel, and prepare you after your
p1323 text    families and kindreds,
p1323 verse   5 According as David the king of Israel prescribed, and according to the
p1323 text    magnificence of Solomon his son: and standing in the temple according to the several
p1323 text    dignity of the families of you the Levites, who minister in the presence of your
p1323 text    brethren the children of Israel,
p1323 verse   6 Offer the passover in order, and make ready the sacrifices for your brethren, and
p1323 text    keep the passover according to the commandment of the Lord, which was given unto
p1323 text    Moses.
p1323 verse   7 And unto the people that was found there Josias gave thirty thousand lambs and
p1323 text    kids, and three thousand calves: these things were given of the king’s allowance,
p1323 text    according as he promised, to the people, to the priests, and to the Levites.
p1323 verse   8 And Helkias, Zacharias, and Syelus, the governors of the temple, gave to the priests
p1323 text    for the passover two thousand and six hundred sheep, and three hundred calves.
p1323 verse   9 And Jeconias, and Samaias, and Nathanael his brother, and Assabias, and Ochiel,
p1323 text    and Joram, captains over thousands, gave to the Levites for the passover five thousand
p1323 text    sheep, and seven hundred calves.
p1323 verse   10 And when these things were done, the priests and Levites, having the unleavened
p1323 text    bread, stood in very comely order according to the kindreds,
p1323 verse   11 And according to the several dignities of the fathers, before the people, to offer to
p1323 text    the Lord, as it is written in the book of Moses: and thus did they in the morning.
p1323 verse   12 And they roasted the passover with fire, as appertaineth: as for the sacrifices, they
p1323 text    sod them in brass pots and pans with a good savour,
p1323 verse   13 And set them before all the people: and afterward they prepared for themselves,
p1323 text    and for the priests their brethren, the sons of Aaron.
p1323 verse   14 For the priests offered the fat until night: and the Levites prepared for themselves,
p1323 text    and the priests their brethren, the sons of Aaron.
p1323 verse   15 The holy singers also, the sons of Asaph, were in their order, according to the
p1323 text    appointment of David, to wit, Asaph, Zacharias, and Jeduthun, who was of the king’s
p1323 text    retinue.
p1323 verse   16 Moreover the porters were at every gate; it was not lawful for any to go from his
p1323 text    ordinary service: for their brethren the Levites prepared for them.
p1323 verse   17 Thus were the things that belonged to the sacrifices of the Lord accomplished in
p1323 text    that day, that they might hold the passover,
p1323 verse   18 And offer sacrifices upon the altar of the Lord, according to the commandment of
p1323 text    king Josias.
p1323 verse   19 So the children of Israel which were present held the passover at that time, and
p1323 text    the feast of sweet bread seven days.
p1323 verse   20 And such a passover was not kept in Israel since the time of the prophet Samuel.

p1324 verse   21 Yea, all the kings of Israel held not such a passover as Josias, and the priests, and
p1324 text    the Levites, and the Jews, held with all Israel that were found dwelling at Jerusalem.
p1324 verse   22 In the eighteenth year of the reign of Josias was this passover kept.
p1324 verse   23 And the works or Josias were upright before his Lord with an heart full of
p1324 text    godliness.
p1324 verse   24 As for the things that came to pass in his time, they were written in former times,
p1324 text    concerning those that sinned, and did wickedly against the Lord above all people and
p1324 text    kingdoms, and how they grieved him exceedingly, so that the words of the Lord rose
p1324 text    up against Israel.
p1324 verse   25 Now after all these acts of Josias it came to pass, that Pharaoh the king of Egypt
p1324 text    came to raise war at Carchamis upon Euphrates: and Josias went out against him.
p1324 verse   26 But the king of Egypt sent to him, saying, What have I to do with thee, O king of
p1324 text    Judea?
p1324 verse   27 I am not sent out from the Lord God against thee; for my war is upon Euphrates:
p1324 text    and now the Lord is with me, yea, the Lord is with me hasting me forward: depart
p1324 text    from me, and be not against the Lord.
p1324 verse   28 Howbeit Josias did not turn back his chariot from him, but undertook to fight with
p1324 text    him, not regarding the words of the prophet Jeremy spoken by the mouth of the Lord:
p1324 verse   29 But joined battle with him in the plain of Magiddo, and the princes came against
p1324 text    king Josias.
p1324 verse   30 Then said the king unto his servants, Carry me away out of the battle; for I am very
p1324 text    weak. And immediately his servants took him away out of the battle.
p1324 verse   31 Then gat he up upon his second chariot; and being brought back to Jerusalem
p1324 text    died, and was buried in his father’s sepulchre.

p1324 text    Josias, and the chief men with the women made lamentation for him unto this day: and

p1324 text    Lord, and the things that he had done before, and the things now recited, are reported

p1324 verse   34 And the people took Joachaz the son of Josias, and made him king instead of Josias
p1324 text    his father, when he was twenty and three years old.
p1324 verse   35 And he reigned in Judea and in Jerusalem three months: and then the king of
p1324 text    Egypt deposed him from reigning in Jerusalem.

p1324 verse   38 And he bound Joacim and the nobles: but Zaraces his brother he apprehended,

p1325 verse   54 And they took all the holy vessels of the Lord, both great and small, with the

p1325 verse   58 Until the land had enjoyed her sabbaths, the whole time of her desolation shall she

p1325 chapter 2
p1325 verse   1 In the first year of Cyrus king of the Persians, that the word of the Lord might be
p1325 text    accomplished, that he had promised by the mouth of Jeremy;

p1325 text    proclamation through all his kingdom, and also by writing,

p1325 text    Lord, hath made me king of the whole world,

p1325 text    with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem that is in Judea, and build the house of the

p1325 text    his neighbours, with gold, and with silver,
p1325 verse   7 With gifts, with horses, and with cattle, and other things, which have been set forth
p1325 text    by vow, for the temple of the Lord at Jerusalem.

p1327 chapter 3
p1327 verse   1 Now when Darius reigned, he made a great feast unto all his subjects, and unto all
p1327 text    his household, and unto all the princes of Media and Persia,
p1327 verse   2 And to all the governors and captains and lieutenants that were under him, from
p1327 text    India unto Ethiopia, of an hundred twenty and seven provinces.
p1327 verse   3 And when they had eaten and drunken, and being satisfied were gone home, then
p1327 text    Darius the king went into his bedchamber, and slept, and soon after awaked.
p1327 verse   4 Then three young men, that were of the guard that kept the king’s body, spake one
p1327 text    to another;
p1327 verse   5 Let every one of us speak a sentence: he that shall overcome, and whose sentence
p1327 text    shall seem wiser than the others, unto him shall the king Darius give great gifts, and
p1327 text    great things in token of victory:
p1327 verse   6 As, to be clothed in purple, to drink in gold, and to sleep upon gold, and a chariot
p1327 text    with bridles of gold, and an headtire of fine linen, and a chain about his neck:
p1327 verse   7 And he shall sit next to Darius because of his wisdom, and shall be called Darius his
p1327 text    cousin.
p1327 verse   8 And then every one wrote his sentence, sealed it, and laid it under king Darius his
p1327 text    pillow;
p1327 verse   9 And said that, when the king is risen, some will give him the writings; and of whose
p1327 text    side the king and the three princes of Persia shall judge that his sentence is the wisest,
p1327 text    to him shall the victory be given, as was appointed.
p1327 verse   10 The first wrote, Wine is the strongest.
p1327 verse   11 The second wrote, The king is strongest.
p1327 verse   12 The third wrote, Women are strongest: but above all things Truth beareth away
p1327 text    the victory.
p1327 verse   13 Now when the king was risen up, they took their writings, and delivered them
p1327 text    unto him, and so he read them:
p1327 verse   14 And sending forth he called all the princes of Persia and Media, and the governors,
p1327 text    and the captains, and the lieutenants, and the chief officers;
p1327 verse   15 And sat him down in the royal seat of judgment; and the writings were read
p1327 text    before them.
p1327 verse   16 And he said, Call the young men, and they shall declare their own sentences. So
p1327 text    they were called, and came in.
p1327 verse   17 And he said unto them, Declare unto us your mind concerning the writings. Then
p1327 text    began the first, who had spoken of the strength of wine;
p1327 verse   18 And he said thus, O ye men, how exceeding strong is wine! it causeth all men to err
p1327 text    that drink it:
p1327 verse   19 It maketh the mind of the king and of the fatherless child to be all one; of the
p1327 text    bondman and of the freeman, of the poor man and of the rich:
p1327 verse   20 It turneth also every thought into jollity and mirth, so that a man remembereth
p1327 text    neither sorrow nor debt:
p1327 verse   21 And it maketh every heart rich, so that a man remembereth neither king nor
p1327 text    governor; and it maketh to speak all things by talents:
p1328 head    1 Esdras 3:22 1324 1 Esdras 4:22
p1328 verse   22 And when they are in their cups, they forget their love both to friends and
p1328 text    brethren, and a little after draw out swords:
p1328 verse   23 But when they are from the wine, they remember not what they have done.
p1328 verse   24 O ye men, is not wine the strongest, that enforceth to do thus? And when he had so
p1328 text    spoken, he held his peace.
p1328 chapter 4
p1328 verse   1 Then the second, that had spoken of the strength of the king, began to say,
p1328 verse   2 O ye men, do not men excel in strength that bear rule over sea and land and all
p1328 text    things in them?
p1328 verse   3 But yet the king is more mighty: for he is lord of all these things, and hath dominion
p1328 text    over them; and whatsoever he commandeth them they do.
p1328 verse   4 If he bid them make war the one against the other, they do it: if he send them out
p1328 text    against the enemies, they go, and break down mountains walls and towers.
p1328 verse   5 They slay and are slain, and transgress not the king’s commandment: if they get the
p1328 text    victory, they bring all to the king, as well the spoil, as all things else.
p1328 verse   6 Likewise for those that are no soldiers, and have not to do with wars, but use
p1328 text    husbundry, when they have reaped again that which they had sown, they bring it to
p1328 text    the king, and compel one another to pay tribute unto the king.
p1328 verse   7 And yet he is but one man: if he command to kill, they kill; if he command to spare,
p1328 text    they spare;
p1328 verse   8 If he command to smite, they smite; if he command to make desolate, they make
p1328 text    desolate; if he command to build, they build;
p1328 verse   9 If he command to cut down, they cut down; if he command to plant, they plant.
p1328 verse   10 So all his people and his armies obey him: furthermore he lieth down, he eateth
p1328 text    and drinketh, and taketh his rest:
p1328 verse   11 And these keep watch round about him, neither may any one depart, and do his
p1328 text    own business, neither disobey they him in any thing.
p1328 verse   12 O ye men, how should not the king be mightiest, when in such sort he is obeyed?
p1328 text    And he held his tongue.
p1328 verse   13 Then the third, who had spoken of women, and of the truth, (this was Zorobabel)
p1328 text    began to speak.
p1328 verse   14 O ye men, it is not the great king, nor the multitude of men, neither is it wine, that
p1328 text    excelleth; who is it then that ruleth them, or hath the lordship over them? are they not
p1328 text    women?
p1328 verse   15 Women have borne the king and all the people that bear rule by sea and land.
p1328 verse   16 Even of them came they: and they nourished them up that planted the vineyards,
p1328 text    from whence the wine cometh.
p1328 verse   17 These also make garments for men; these bring glory unto men; and without
p1328 text    women cannot men be.
p1328 verse   18 Yea, and if men have gathered together gold and silver, or any other goodly thing,
p1328 text    do they not love a woman which is comely in favour and beauty?
p1328 verse   19 And letting all those things go, do they not gape, and even with open mouth fix
p1328 text    their eyes fast on her; and have not all men more desire unto her than unto silver or
p1328 text    gold, or any goodly thing whatsoever?
p1328 verse   20 A man leaveth his own father that brought him up, and his own country, and
p1328 text    cleaveth unto his wife.
p1328 verse   21 He sticketh not to spend his life with his wife. and remembereth neither father,
p1328 text    nor mother, nor country.
p1328 verse   22 By this also ye must know that women have dominion over you: do ye not labour
p1328 text    and toil, and give and bring all to the woman?

p1329 verse   40 Neither in her judgment is any unrighteousness; and she is the strength, kingdom,
p1329 text    power, and majesty, of all ages. Blessed be the God of truth.
p1329 verse   41 And with that he held his peace. And all the people then shouted, and said, Great is

p1343 head    Manasseh 1 1339 Manasseh 15
p1343 title   The Prayer of Manasseh, or, The Prayer of Manasses
p1343 title   King of Judah
p1343 verse   1 O Lord, Almighty God of our fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and of their
p1343 text    righteous seed;
p1343 verse   2 who hast made heaven and earth, with all the ornament thereof;
p1343 verse   3 who hast bound the sea by the word of thy commandment; who hast shut up the
p1343 text    deep, and sealed it by thy terrible and glorious name;
p1343 verse   4 whom all men fear, and tremble before thy power;
p1343 verse   5 for the majesty of thy glory cannot be borne, and thine angry threatening toward
p1343 text    sinners is importable:
p1343 verse   6 but thy merciful promise is unmeasurable and unsearchable;
p1343 verse   7 for thou art the most high Lord, of great compassion, longsuffering, very merciful,
p1343 text    and repentest of the evils of men. Thou, O Lord, according to thy great goodness hast
p1343 text    promised repentance and forgiveness to them that have sinned against thee: and of
p1343 text    thine infinite mercies hast appointed repentance unto sinners, that they may be saved.
p1343 verse   8 Thou therefore, O Lord, that art the God of the just, hast not appointed repentance
p1343 text    to the just, as to Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, which have not sinned against thee;
p1343 text    but thou hast appointed repentance unto me that am a sinner:
p1343 verse   9 for I have sinned above the number of the sands of the sea. My transgressions, O
p1343 text    Lord, are multiplied: my transgressions are multiplied, and I am not worthy to behold
p1343 text    and see the height of heaven for the multitude of mine iniquities.
p1343 verse   10 I am bowed down with many iron bands, that I cannot lift up mine head, neither
p1343 text    have any release: for I have provoked thy wrath, and done evil before thee: I did not
p1343 text    thy will, neither kept I thy commandments: I have set up abominations, and have
p1343 text    multiplied offences.
p1343 verse   11 Now therefore I bow the knee of mine heart, beseeching thee of grace.
p1343 verse   12 I have sinned, O Lord, I have sinned, and I acknowledge mine iniquities:
p1343 verse   13 wherefore, I humbly beseech thee, forgive me, O Lord, forgive me, and destroy me
p1343 text    not with mine iniquites. Be not angry with me for ever, by reserving evil for me;
p1343 text    neither condemn me to the lower parts of the earth. For thou art the God, even the God
p1343 text    of them that repent;
p1343 verse   14 and in me thou wilt shew all thy goodness: for thou wilt save me, that am
p1343 text    unworthy, according to thy great mercy.
p1343 verse   15 Therefore I will praise thee for ever all the days of my life: for all the powers of the
p1343 text    heavens do praise thee, and thine is the glory for ever and ever. Amen.
